title: perf(adaptive): simplify growth outlines before opening
body:
The actual STEP bore spent 277.759 s in its release import/generate/verify test on the frozen baseline. With this change repeated release/debug tests pass in 5.866/31.308 s. Observed bounds on this Linux i7-1360P are 15 s release and 40 s debug for the complete test, including every growth level; these are measured bounds, not universal real-time guarantees.

Simplify each growth opening's input at 0.25 um using iterative Ramer/Douglas-Peucker, erode an extra 0.51 um, and intersect the result with the original region. The intersection is the containment backstop; approximate simplification does not inherit the exact opening's nesting proof. Invalid simplifications or changed loop/hole counts fall back to the original outline. Load, travel and geometry budget limits and final path guards are unchanged.

Independent verification on Linux x86-64:

- Actual STEP bore: baseline 15561/14837/1561 moves/planar-feeds/arcs; candidate 16029/15372/1427 in release and debug. The first candidate run failed only the old exact-count pin after its safety checks; only the measured Linux triple is updated, and the repeated release test passes.
- Six planar adaptive fixtures pass: bore R12.5, rectangle and L-pocket unchanged; narrow slot stays HSM with 0 in-cut breaks, 14262 -> 14664 moves and 15.4 -> 15.7 % D load. Island and channel retain their named Offset rings fallbacks (100 % D and 42/40 breaks, existing fallback behavior, not HSM-law successes).
- All six rotary fixtures pass with no new fallback/refusal: bar's deepest band 18.4 -> 18.0 % D, window's deeper bands 18.4 % D, neck bands 17.3/17.7 % D; no in-cut break over 5 degrees. Fitted arcs/move counts change; the Offset rings digest is unchanged.
- Both annular-band refusal tests and all four motion stepped-pocket tests pass. Small-helix crossing regression passes. Seven new simplification tests pass in release/debug, including whole-region difference containment for acute notches, nearby components, thin walls/holes/nested islands, cyclic seams and degenerates. The 56 s debug growth-cost pin remains covered in the explicitly named heavy lane; the six defaults pass in 15.16 s.
- Motion/app clippy `--all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` pass (271 default tests, 12 ignored heavy, 51 s, no VOID). Full release adaptive-unit run passes: frozen baseline 45 tests in 314.244 s, candidate 52 in 244.970 s, including budget twins and twenty slot perturbations.

Full fixture count/load/break comparisons, commands, timing caveats and rejected alternatives are in the [decision record](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/issue/882-adaptive-opening/docs/decisions/882-adaptive-open-simplify.md). No safety thresholds are relaxed to accept a changed plan.

Limitations: Windows/macOS were not run; their previously measured exact STEP triples remain unchanged and need remeasurement on those platforms. Graphify is unavailable on PATH. No snapshot or golden files change.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, process version 52. The issue branch alone merges upstream main for the already-landed blockers; baseline tree equals upstream `4c229ed3`. Fork main stays on the released product baseline.

Changelog: adaptive ring opening avoids repeated fine-outline offsets while preserving containment and safety checks.

title: fix(wire): stamp the wire contour's side by its own value and an open run's clearance
body:
## What changed

`OpParams::stamp_with`, Wire Contour arm (`crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`): the side was written as `u8::from(side == Punch)`, so Die, Left and Right digested alike, and the run-out clearance was never written. An open run turned left <-> right, or given a new clearance, kept its stamp, so its old path (kerf on the side the user no longer states) read Ok and could post.

The side now writes its own discriminant, and an open run also writes its clearance:

| Side | Bytes written |
|---|---|
| Die | `0` (as before) |
| Punch | `1` (as before) |
| Left | `2`, then the clearance |
| Right | `3`, then the clearance |

**Existing stamps:** die and punch stamps are byte-identical to before, so no closed cut goes Stale on upgrade, and a closed cut's clearance (which it never reads) still moves nothing. An open (Left/Right) run generated before this change reads Stale once after load and clears on regenerate. That is the one-time churn every stamp change causes. No golden or roundtrip fixture pins a wire stamp value: no committed `.ccam`/JSON fixture holds a `wire_contour`, and `golden_cl` pins CL output, not stamps.

The change is limited to the one stamp arm, plus a new test file. Open wire PRs #1163, #1181 and #1218 touch or move the same arm (they add `taper_deg` next to it and keep the old `== Punch` byte). Whichever merges second keeps both changes.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/wire_stamp.rs`:
- `an_open_runs_side_and_clearance_each_mark_its_path_stale`: a generated open cut-off is saved, its side is turned (and, separately, its clearance re-stated) in the file, and it is reopened with its old path and stamp. It reads Stale in both cases. Through the commands, the edit reads Stale and undo reads Ok.
- `the_four_sides_stamp_apart_and_a_closed_cut_ignores_the_clearance`: all four sides give distinct `current_stamp`s. Die and punch ignore the clearance. Left and right read it.
- `an_unrelated_edit_and_a_round_trip_leave_the_cuts_ok`: another operation's edit, a closed punch's clearance re-stated in its file, and a plain save/load all leave the cuts Ok.

The first two tests fail on `upstream/main` without the fix (checked by reverting `params.rs`), and all three pass with it.

Suites run green: `wire_stamp`, `wire_contour`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_post`, `wire_readers`, `wire_verify`, `project_roundtrip`, `operations`, `golden_cl`. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` both pass on the final head.

**Why the file door:** `EditOperationParams` drops the stamp on every edit, so an edit always reads Stale and cannot prove the digest. The paths that keep a stamp are a project file and the stored stamp it reloads, so the pin goes through the file.

## Not exercised

The GUI wire page, and a real EDM control.

Changelog: An open wire run edited left <-> right, or given a new run-out clearance, now reads Stale instead of keeping its old path (#1370)

title: fix(post): refuse a cut with the spindle stopped in every spindle mill dialect
body:
**Stacked on #1367** (branch `issue/1357-cycle-feed-spindle`). Retarget this PR to `main` before #1367 merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0; branch merged with upstream main through #1367's branch.

## What changed
- **The spindle rule in every spindle mill dialect.** #1357 gave `tormach.cps` a spindle-state rule, and the #1367 review fixed its touch-probe exemption. That rule is now ported to `fanuc`, `haas`, `sinumerik`, `mazak`, `heidenhain`, `doosan-dnm`, `grblhal`, `tinyg` and `carvera`.
  - Each post tracks `spindleOn` from its preamble's spindle start (`S.. M3`; Mazak `MOTON S..`; Carvera `M3 S..`) to the next stop: every section end, and a touch probe's stop.
  - A feed, arc or canned cycle with the spindle stopped is refused by name and nothing is posted for it, e.g. `feed move G1 with the spindle stopped - no spindle start (S.. M3) precedes it; state the operation's spindle speed`. One message per program.
  - **Probe exemption:** the section must state 0 rpm **and** `PARAM ToolKind touch probe`. A cutter at 0 rpm, or a 0-rpm section that states no tool kind, is refused. The kind resets at every section end.
  - **tinyg and carvera** write no canned cycles; their holes are plain feeds, so the feed check covers holes.
  - **Heidenhain** checks its native cycle last, after the tapping refusals. A tap with no spindle speed keeps its own refusal ("tapping needs a positive integral spindle speed"). The cycle stays open, so the hole's chain is swallowed, not posted.
- **Exempt posts:**
  - `tormach-plasma` and `wire-iso` have no spindle.
  - `fanuc-lathe` and `tormach-lathe` do not share the mill pattern, and they already refuse a cut with no spindle speed their own way:
    - feed per rev (G99) needs a spindle speed;
    - fanuc-lathe's only feed-per-minute mode (G98, C-axis live tooling) needs a live-tool speed.
  - So no lathe post changed.
- **Fixtures:**
  - `conformance.rs` now posts every mill dialect's golden from `as_program` (`tests/common/legacy_program.rs`): tool change, spindle speed, setup/operation/tool comments and cycle feeds, on the same generic VMC. The pinned `.cl` files are untouched.
  - `legacy_program::operation_for` gains a `trochoid_` arm (6 mm end mill, "Trochoidal slot").
  - These hand-written streams gain a `SpindleSpeed`:
    - post crate: `fanuc_post`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `arc_planes`, `axis_direction_cli`;
    - app: `fourth_axis_pose`, `tinyg_post`.
  - `heidenhain_block_form` uses `as_program`, and so does `program_units`' grbl-family test, plus the `ClearancePlane` a real stream states (both posts lift to it at a tool change).
- **Decisions:** `docs/decisions/1359-spindle-rule-all.md`.

## Goldens moved: 115 files, regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`
**Only added lines.** Diffed with the N block numbers stripped, **0 lines were removed or changed** across all 115 files. The added lines are:
- the setup, operation and tool comments;
- the tool change, in each dialect's own form: `T.. M6` + `G43 H..`; Sinumerik `T.. D.. M6`; Heidenhain `T.. G17 S..`; Carvera `M6 T..`; TinyG `M5`/`M9`/lift/`T.. M6`/`M0`/frame restate;
- the spindle start: `S.. M3`, or Mazak `MOTON S..`, Carvera `M3 S..`, Heidenhain `M3`.

Heidenhain and Sinumerik renumber their N words.

- **fanuc** (top level, 14): contour_disc_hole, contour_plate_with_hole, contour_tangential_lead, drill_peck, drill_plate, face_square_40x40, face_square_40x40_stepped, pocket_waterline_plate_with_island, pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island, slot_fullwidth_centerline, slot_wide_channel_rows, tap_plate, trace_plate_with_hole, trochoid_slot_small
- **haas** (13): the 13 conformance goldens (the 13 above, without trochoid)
- **sinumerik** (13): the same 13
- **mazak** (13): the same 13
- **doosan-dnm** (13): the same 13
- **heidenhain** (12 changed + 1 new): the 12 without tap_plate changed. **`heidenhain/tap_plate.nc` is new.** That golden was a named refusal (`REFUSED`) only because the bare stream stated no spindle speed. With 500 rpm stated (the M10x1.5 tap: 750 mm/min over a 1.5 mm pitch) it posts G207, so its `REFUSED` entry is gone.
- **grblhal** (12), **tinyg** (12), **carvera** (12): the 12 without tap_plate. tap_plate stays refused by name there: no G84, or no spindle reverse.
- **tormach:** no golden moved.

## Pins: `crates/app/tests/post_spindle_rule_all.rs`, table-driven over the 9 dialects
- `a_feed_with_no_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name_in_every_dialect`: refused once, and the same section with a spindle speed posts clean.
- `an_arc_with_no_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name_in_every_dialect`
- `a_hole_with_no_spindle_start_is_refused_by_name_in_every_dialect`: a canned cycle (Heidenhain: its drilling cycle; tinyg/carvera: the plunge feed). With a spindle it posts clean.
- `a_cutter_stating_zero_rpm_is_refused_and_a_touch_probe_is_not`: a cutter at 0 rpm and a 0-rpm section with no kind are refused; a touch probe at 0 rpm is exempt; a no-kind 0-rpm section after a probe section is refused again.
- `a_section_after_the_stop_that_states_no_speed_is_refused`

**Mutations** (the post file is edited and the pin binary re-run; every mutant is caught):

| Mutant | Fails |
|---|---|
| Rule off (`spindleStopped` never refuses), in each of the 9 posts, one at a time | all 5 pins, each time |
| fanuc: the cycle check dropped | the hole pin |
| heidenhain: the cycle check dropped | the hole pin |
| haas: the arc check dropped | the arc pin |
| mazak: exemption on 0 rpm alone (the pre-review Tormach bug) | the 0-rpm pin |
| grblhal: probe never exempt | the 0-rpm pin |
| sinumerik: the tool kind not reset at section end | the 0-rpm pin (the probe-then-no-kind case) |
| doosan-dnm: M5 not clearing `spindleOn` | the section-after-stop pin |
| tinyg: M3 not setting `spindleOn` | 3 pins |

## How tested
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` at b0d50c6f is green: post suites ok, app suites ok (548 s).
- camcraft-post: all suites pass.
- App: `conformance`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle`, `tinyg_post`, `fourth_axis_pose` and `golden_cl` pass. Before the merge of main, the whole camcraft-app test set (every binary) ran green after the two fixture fixes.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- The `--ignored` heavy lanes and the release-tier UI snapshot lane.
- **No controller run.** The changed goldens are for the generic VMC dialects, not the 770MX, so no Hub run applies.
- A mid-section `SpindleSpeed` change still takes effect only at the next preamble. This was pre-existing and is unchanged here.

Changelog: Every spindle mill post (Fanuc, Haas, Siemens 840D, Mazak, Heidenhain, Doosan DNM, grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera) refuses a feed, arc or canned cycle with the spindle stopped by name; a touch-probe section is exempt only on a touch-probe tool.
Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(post): refuse a canned cycle with no feed and a Tormach cut with the spindle stopped
body:
## What changed

**Refusals (Prime Directive: refuse by name instead of posting something silently wrong)**
- **A canned cycle with no feed is refused by name.** If `FeedRate` is missing or not > 0, the post emits `canned cycle G73 has no feed rate - refused: ...` through the post's `msg()` / `refuse()` path and writes no G7x/G8x. This applies to every post that writes a cycle with its own F: `tormach`, `fanuc`, `haas`, `sinumerik`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm`, `grblhal` and `fanuc-lathe`.
- **heidenhain** keeps its fallback to the hole chain's own feed (`ChainFeedRate`), but no longer falls back to the program's last modal feed. With neither feed, its existing "missing/invalid positive cutting feed" refusal fires.
- **tinyg, carvera and tormach-lathe** post drilling as plain chain moves with their own F, so they need no change.
- **`tormach.cps`: a cut with the spindle stopped is refused by name.** This covers G1, G2/G3 and canned cycles: `feed move G1 in operation X with the spindle stopped - no spindle start (S.. M3) precedes it; ...`.
  - `spindleOn` is true from the preamble's `S.. M3` to the next `M5`. Every section ends in M5, so a later section that states no speed is refused too.
  - A touch-probe section (a stated 0 rpm, #574) is exempt.
  - The other spindle mill posts get the same rule in follow-up **#1359** (P2, effort:high, area:post). Every one of their conformance goldens is a bare legacy stream with no spindle, so doing it here would move about 120 more goldens.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` states the new law.

**Goldens**
- The `.cl` goldens are generator outputs that `golden_cl.rs` pins, so they are not edited. Instead, the new `crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs` builds the streams the tests post:
  - `with_cycle_feeds`: each `; CYCLE` marker gets its own chain's cutting feed. This is what `post::dump` synthesizes for a generated cycle.
  - `as_program`: also prepends the records a real operation's stream carries: SetupName, OperationName, OperationKind, ToolKind, ToolDiameter, `TOOL`, `SpindleSpeed`.
  - The post crate's `fanuc_post.rs` and `arc_planes.rs` include the same file by path, so the shared `nc/*.nc` goldens come from one stream.
- **The Tormach goldens are runnable programs.** `conformance.rs` now posts the Tormach mill goldens for the **770MX** (`tormach-770mx.mch`, inch) instead of the generic `3axis-vmc.mch`. They now open `(Tormach 770MX)` and carry:
  - `(SETUP: Setup1)`, `(OPERATION: Drill1 - DRILL - G54)` and `(T4 6MM HSS DRILL - DRILL D0.2362)`;
  - `G53 G0 Z0` / `G30` / `T4 M6` / `G43 H4` / `S1500 M3`;
  - an F on the G73 (`G73 X0.7874 Y0.3937 Z-0.9449 R0 Q0.7087 F2.36`) and on the tap (`G84 ... F29.53`, a 1.5 mm pitch at 500 rpm).
  - The tool diameters are the ones `golden_cl.rs` generated each path with.
- **`index_4face_microarc4.nc` showed the bug itself.** Its hand-built stream stated the spindle once. The old golden then cut sections 2-4 after their predecessor's M5 with no restart. The test stream now states `SpindleSpeed` per section, as `post::dump` does, and the golden gains `S6000 M3` (and the belt note) in each section.

### Goldens regenerated (WRITE_GOLDEN=1)
- `nc/drill_peck.nc`, `nc/drill_plate.nc`, `nc/tap_plate.nc` (Fanuc): an F on each cycle block, nothing else.
- `nc/haas/`, `nc/mazak/`, `nc/sinumerik/`, `nc/doosan-dnm/`: `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `tap_plate`. An F on each cycle block, nothing else.
- `nc/grblhal/drill_peck.nc`, `nc/grblhal/drill_plate.nc`: an F on each cycle block (grblhal refuses the tap, so it has no tap golden).
- `nc/tormach/`: all 13 legacy goldens (`contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole`). These are now inch programs for the 770MX with the full preamble.
- `nc/tormach/index_4face_microarc4.nc`: `S6000 M3` in sections 2-4 (above).
- heidenhain, tinyg and carvera goldens did not move. No UI snapshot PNG was touched.

### Tests updated to post real programs
`tormach_post.rs`, `tormach_end_units.rs`, `tormach_machines.rs` (`tap_on`) and `tormach_fourth_axis.rs` (a `SpindleSpeed` per section) used bare legacy streams. They now use `as_program`. Their assertions are unchanged, except `an_inch_machine_posts_every_length_and_feed_in_inches`: it skips the 770MX's belt-range note line, because the metric reference machine states no belt ranges.

Each one fails when its fix is mutated away:
- `a_canned_cycle_with_no_feed_is_refused_by_name`: every cycle post. It fails with the tormach check disabled, with the fanuc check disabled, and with any heidenhain fallback put back.

title: test(setup): pin that undoing DeleteSetup keeps the setup order and the posted program
body:
## What changed

The reported bug does not reproduce, so there is no code change. Instead, new tests pin the contract the issue asks for.

- **How setup order is stored:** it is the name order. `setup::setups` reads `model::named_entities`, which sorts by name. No index field, list component or entity-id order holds it. When undo re-spawns a deleted setup, it sorts back into its old place. The operation order (`setup::operation_order`, ranked by setup) and the post follow from that.
- **Where the report came from:** PR #1361's MCP test made "Front" then "Back" and saw `["Back", "Front"]` after the undo. That was already the order before the delete (name order, not creation order). The setup did not move.
- New suite `crates/app/tests/setup_delete_order.rs`:
  - `undoing_delete_of_a_middle_setup_restores_its_place_and_the_program` sets up three setups, created out of name order (`A_First`, `C_Last`, then `B_Middle`). Each has its own stock, and Face ops sit in the first and last. It deletes `B_Middle` and undoes, then asserts the setup names, the active setup, the operation order, and that the **full posted G-code text** equals the program posted before the delete. It then redoes, which deletes the setup again, and undoes again.
  - `undoing_delete_of_the_first_setup_puts_it_back_first` checks that the setup `None` resolves to comes back first after undo.
- `docs/decisions/1362-delete-setup-undo-order.md` records this finding.

## Related commands checked

- `CreateSetup` undo removes the setup it made.
- A datum-transfer clone is a `CreateSetup`; its undo is pinned by `setups::datum_transfer_clones_the_world_and_undoes_exactly`.
- Main has no setup reorder or setup rename command, so nothing else can move a setup.
- If an explicit, hand-set setup position is added later, these tests fail when its undo loses the position.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran app:`setup_delete_order` (2 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Both tests also pass on unchanged main, which is the finding.

title: fix(verify): the mid-turn overhang backstop reads the whole turn
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. **Stacked on #1319** (#1313's swept cells, not yet on main): this branch is based on `issue/1313-midturn-swept-band`; its own change is the last commit.

## What changed

Law (c3)'s overhang backstop - stock hidden under a ledge, which no column sample sees - still asked 4 path stations x 5 turn fractions per band, each at that pose's bottom plane. A holder or shank swinging through hidden stock between two of those poses got no `SweepHit` (#1316).

It now asks over the same reachable set #1313's column law reads, on its own coarser cells:

- New module `crates/sim/src/verify/turn_hidden.rs`. Per live band, #1313's cells (hull of the column's two end discs, grown by the proven sag, swept along each tip chord) with the turn split so the sag is at most 0.05 mm (`BACKSTOP_SAG`, a tenth of the hidden law's 0.5 mm XY spacing), capped at 20 intervals (`BACKSTOP_PLANES`). The tip's chords are grouped into at most 4 runs, and at most `20 / intervals` of them.
- One ask per (interval, run): at the lowest bottom any column of its cells reaches, over the union of their footprints. A point counts only where some position of a cell stands the band over it outside the flutes' kerf at that same tip position (`Cell::bottom_over`, unchanged).
- New entry point `Rest::hidden_in_cover` in `hidden.rs`: the hidden region's boundary samples in the box, plus footprint probes (disc centres and rings at 5 tip positions per chord, built only when the plane has hidden stock near the box), filtered by that membership. A failed slice still convicts.
- `turn_cells.rs`: `push_cells_with` (a stated sag budget and cap; `push_cells` keeps 0.001 mm / 64), `Cell::floor`, `Cell::probes`, `Cell::interval`. `sweep.rs` drops `backstop_columns`, `path_point` and the 4 x 5 grid.

**Slice count per move:** at most 20 distinct planes per live band (`BACKSTOP_PLANES`), the same as the old 4 x 5 grid, so the slicing budget does not change. Pinned by the unit test `a_move_asks_at_most_twenty_planes_per_band`. Past the cap the cells only grow: a 90 degree turn at 150 mm reach overstates by 0.12 mm, still on the safe side.

## How tested

- `crates/sim/tests/midturn_hidden_backstop.rs` - `a_holder_crossing_hidden_stock_between_two_sampled_poses_is_convicted`: a holder 100 mm up the stack swings B 0 -> 80 under a ledge. title: fix(verify): the mid-turn sweep reads the whole turn, not five poses
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Reach law (c3), the mid-turn sweep, read the band stack's column at 4 path stations x 5 turn fractions. Between them a holder or shank could cross uncut stock with no `SweepHit` (#1313).

It now reads the whole reachable set, by construction:

- New module `crates/sim/src/verify/turn_cells.rs`. Per band, one *cell* per tip chord and per interval of the turn. A cell is the convex hull of law (c)'s column at the interval's two end poses, grown by a proven sag, with its bottom at the lower end bottom less the sag.
- The sag bound: the letters lerp and bend the axis no faster than their own sweep, so inside a cell the axis strays from the chord of its end axes by at most `(sweep in the cell)^2 / 8`; times the band's reach above the tip. The cell count keeps it at 0.001 mm or less, capped at 64 cells per band (a 90 degree turn at 150 mm reach then overstates by 0.011 mm, still conservative).
- The tip's travel is not sampled either: the hull is clipped against the tip chord exactly, the bottom rides the chord's Z, and the flutes' kerf excuses a column only for the tip positions that stand over it.
- `sweep.rs` asks a cell one question (`bottom_over`); the column memo and the worst-offender rule are unchanged. `midpose::pose` became `pub(super)` to share the letter lerp.

A refusal is the safe side here: the new reading is a superset of the old one at every pose and station the old grid read.

## How tested

- `crates/sim/tests/midturn_swept_band.rs` - `a_holder_crossing_a_stock_post_between_two_sampled_poses_is_convicted`: a holder 100 mm up the stack swings through a stock post between the 20 and 40 degree samples of an 80 degree turn. Run against main's `sweep.rs` it reports nothing; here it reports `SweepHit { at: 0 }`. Its twin `a_turn_that_stops_short_of_the_post_stays_clean` keeps a clear swing clean.
- `verify::turn_cells::tests::no_band_position_of_a_random_turn_lies_outside_the_cells` - the issue's brute-force probe: 240 random turns (A and B up to +-85 degrees, a third also in C), 5,076,000 band positions (the true cylinder's surface and law (c)'s own column, 9 path stations x 25 turn fractions). Zero outside the cells, in XY and in Z. The old grid misses 272,961 of the same positions.
- Three more unit tests: the sag bound at a wall, the kerf following the tip, degenerate bands and non-finite letters.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: sim, motion and app suites green (48 gate-mapped suites, every existing mid-turn test, no assertion edited). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- The release lanes (`--ignored`, the big posed fixtures) were not run, so false convictions on real 5-axis programs are not measured. In the debug suites there are none.
- Verify time on a large posed program was not measured. A small turn needs fewer cells than the old 20 states per band; a large one up to 64.
- The overhang backstop (stock hidden under a ledge) still asks the old 4 x 5 grid: filed as #1316.

Decision note: `docs/decisions/1313-midturn-swept-band.md`.

Changelog: Verify's mid-turn sweep (law c3) reads every pose and tip position of a turn instead of five sampled poses, so a holder or shank crossing stock between samples is reported

title: feat(ui,app): an async file picker opens models and projects in the browser
body:
Part of #31, the app and UI on wasm. This slice adds an **async file picker**, so a model or a project can be opened in the browser build. Until now every picker there answered "cancelled".

Fork synced at v0.18.0. The branch merges `upstream/main` (53a52f88) so that it diffs clean against `main`.

## What changed
- **`crates/ui/src/file_pick.rs`** (new): the browser picker. On wasm32, `open()` makes an `<input type=file>` whose `accept` comes from the dialog's filters, clicks it and returns at once. When the user has chosen, the file's name and bytes go into a thread-local inbox, and the next frame is woken through the egui context, which `shell_web` registers.
  - Files over 256 MiB (`BROWSER_READ_LIMIT`) are refused by name before they are read. A failed allocation in wasm aborts the tab.
  - The input and its change closure are held in one slot until the next pick, not `forget`ed, so a cancelled picker does not leak.
  - The inbox, `accept_attr` and `too_big` are plain Rust on every target.
- **`crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs`** (new):
  - `open_model_dialog` / `open_project_dialog`: rfd's synchronous dialog on native (unchanged), the async picker on wasm32.
  - Each frame, `drain_actions` turns every inbox entry into a `CommandKind::OpenPicked`. A model goes through `ImportModel::from_bytes` and `finish_import`: one undo step, and a same-named model is an update. A project goes through `project::open_noted`.
  - A failed read, a refused import, or a project that is not text or not JSON is said on the status line ("import refused: …" / "open failed: …") and changes nothing.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`**: `ImportModel::from_bytes(file_name, data, budget)`. It shares the path import's laws through `checked_budget`: IGES and unknown extensions refused, the STEP budget's bounds. It adds the `MAX_FILE_BYTES` cap and the finite-mesh gate. `geometry::import::parse_model_graded_within` is now `pub`.
- **`crates/ui/src/state.rs`**:
  - Two new `CommandKind` arms route to the functions above.
  - The model and project dialogs' filters are factored out (`mesh_dialog`, `project_dialog`) so both pickers ask with the same ones.
  - `open_project_path`'s reset is factored out as `reset_for_open`, so the bytes open retires the old document the same way. Behaviour is unchanged.
- No dependency added. The picker uses `eframe::web_sys` features that eframe already enables (`HtmlInputElement`, `File`, `FileList`, `Blob`).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-file-picker.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests:
  - `crates/app/tests/import_bytes.rs`:
    - `picked_bytes_import_like_the_same_file_from_disk`: the same name, mesh and fidelity as the disk import, for STL, OBJ and STEP.
    - `picked_bytes_are_refused_by_name_never_a_panic`: IGES, an unknown extension, no extension, empty or corrupt files of each format, and a budget given for a non-STEP file.
  - `crates/ui/src/file_pick_tests.rs`:
    - `a_picked_model_imports_through_the_undoable_command`
    - `a_picked_file_that_cannot_be_used_is_refused_by_name`
    - `a_picked_project_opens_in_place_of_the_document`
    - `the_browser_picker_accepts_the_dialogs_extensions`
    - `a_file_over_the_browser_read_limit_is_refused_before_it_is_read`
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. The app suites (lib, import_bytes, large_models, model_fidelity, step_*, stock_export, bore_facet_sagitta) passed in 21 s. The ui suites (lib, boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, theme_files) passed in 19 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (native, macOS).
- **wasm check**: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` passed on macOS, using the official rustc 1.99.1 with the wasm32 std and Homebrew LLVM's clang for the wasi C.
  - It linked `camcraft-cli.wasm` and `camcraft_ui.wasm`, ran wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and laid out `target/web`. The shim answers all nine WASI imports.
  - camcraft-ui raised no warnings.

  - The script needed two local workarounds, which are not part of this PR: a GNU-`sed -i` shim, and a bash-3.2 empty-array fix for `"${PROFILE_ARGS[@]}"` under `set -u` (line 104). As shipped, the script does not run on stock macOS bash/sed. Worth a small follow-up.

  - The other pickers: fixture import, machine, post, theme and tool library.

title: feat(thread): thread-milling pass control - decreasing passes, finish and spring passes, depth allowance, M4 cutters
body:
Stack order: #1005 (merged) -> #1045 (merged) -> #1137 (open, issue/985-external-threads @ 4f15b9b3) -> this PR. Merge #1137 first; this branch already carries its head. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Thread milling (internal and external) gains pass control, one value `ThreadPasses` on the kernel's `ThreadParams` and on `OpParams::Thread`:

- **Decreasing pass depths (constant chip area)**: `pass_schedule: constant_area` - cumulative depth after pass i of n is `D x sqrt(i/n)`, the infeed is the first (largest) pass, `n = ceil((D/infeed)^2)`, capped at 64 (refused by name past that). The last roughing pass lands exactly on D.
- **Finishing pass** of its own radial depth (`finish_depth`) and **spring passes** (`spring_passes`, at most 4) on the final radius.
- **Depth allowance** (`depth_allowance`, radial): the last pass lands on standard depth - allowance. A negative allowance (past the major diameter of a hole / the design root of a boss) and one over a quarter of the thread depth are refused by name.
- **Spindle and cutter hand** (`spindle_reverse` = M4, `cutter_left_hand`): climb sense flips under M4 (the helix keeps the drawing's hand); a right-hand-cut mill under M4 or a left-hand-cut one under M3 is refused by name. M4 reaches the post via a new `PARAM MillSpindle reverse` (`post::ask_reverse_spindle`) and manifest flag `millSpindleReverse`; `fanuc.cps` declares it and writes `M4`; the engine refuses such a section by name for every other script (the lathe's #629 `SpindleDirection`/`threadHands` is deliberately not reused).
- Gated at the door (create, edit, retool via `thread_op::door`) and again in the kernel. File/MCP keys flattened into the Thread params, additive, written only when not default; the digest clause appears only when not default. Page: Passes tab (schedule, finish, spring, allowance), Feeds tab (spindle, cutter hand).

Defaults are the #894 ride: every existing thread golden (`.cl` and `.nc`) is byte-identical.

## Sources

Smid, "CNC Programming Handbook" (thread cutting: constant-area pass depths, spring pass); Machinery's Handbook ("Thread milling", "Thread cutting": finish pass, climb vs cutter rotation, cutter hand vs spindle); ISO 724 / ISO 965-1 (depths, tolerance scale). title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
Stacked on #1181 (on #1163, #1144, #1139, #1123, #560, #551)

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.

title: fix(motion): land a rapid only on swept stock; hold the developed band's bore exit and lap kinks to the bar's laws
body:
Stacked on #1138 (on #1080, #1007). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

**#1169 - a rapid landed on a wall strip thinner than a planner cell (safety floor).**
The microlift plan read its landings on the planner's cell bitmap (D/120 = 0.083 mm). A wall strip thinner than a cell that falls between two rows of cell centers is invisible there: the easing laps drop it as "air" and it stands until the last lap. On the narrow slot 14x60 the return over the retract plane (`LinkLaw::high`) rapided to 0.3 mm over the floor at (17.407, 8.956) with a 0.075 mm strip under its rim - the verifier's `RapidInStock`.

- New `adaptive::lift_swept::Swept`: the segments the plan's pieces have cut so far, exactly. `high` lands only where the whole footprint (r - 10 um, the verifier's own footprint) is within r - 12.5 um of a cut segment (2.5 um arc fit + the 10 um chords the verifier reads a posted arc on). The proof is a quadtree over the disc on exact segment distances (1-Lipschitz bound per square, divided to 1 um); where it does not close the landing is refused. Nothing is sampled. The cell test stays as the cheap first reading. The verifier is untouched.
- The hop's landing (`lift_link::landing`) takes a lead point the pieces swept before one only the cells read clear. The hop comes down at plunge feed from over the stock, never in rapid, so with no point proved the cells' choice stands.
- A piece starting exactly where the tool stands is ridden on to at the floor (`lift::ride`) instead of a retract and plunge on one spot. That hop, not the strip, was the slot's "4 descents for 2 levels" (the growth's last piece handing over to the first easing lap at (5.135, 7.312), both in cut).

**#1050 - the held fix (16e129bb), now landable.** `adaptive::conform`: the disc phase out of the entry bore is held on the planner's rim and on a rim twice as coarse (the worse kept); the closing laps' fillet kinks are spread at 4 degrees. The measured pins `R62_LOAD_FACTOR`, `R62_BREAKS` and `BAR_50_BREAKS` are removed; the pins hold the whole bar's laws. No law and no bound loosened.

## Readings (release, Linux x86-64)

Narrow slot 14x60, with #1050's change:

| | verifier | descents (2 levels) | returns | over the retract plane | rides | hops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1 `RapidInStock` | 4 | 200 | 3 | 0 | 1 |
| after | silent | 2 | 199 (1365 mm lifted) | 0 | 2 | 0 |

Out of cut 0.88x the cut (law 1.5), load 15.4 % D, 0 breaks, 14262 moves.

Rotary bars (0.1 mm dexel, law 19.8 % D, no break past 5 deg):

| level | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| r6.2 / 5.7 | 20.3 % D, 0 breaks | 17.3 % D, 0 breaks |
| r6.2 / 5.2 | 20.3 % D, 3 breaks | 17.7 % D, 0 breaks |
| r7 / 6.5, 6.0 | - | 19.5 % D, 0 breaks |
| r7 / 5.5, 5.0 | - | 17.3 %, 18.4 % D, 0 breaks |

Other `adaptive_hsm` fixtures: bore 15.4 % D, rectangle 15.4, L-pocket 15.7, 0 breaks, 2 descents each; island and channel fall back to Offset rings as before.

## Verdict moves

- Narrow slot: `RapidInStock` -> silent; its three returns over the retract plane (leads along the walls, not provable at 12.5 um) became routed lifted returns; one retract hop became a ride.
- r6.2 neck levels and r7 level 5.0: measured pins removed, now under the whole bar's laws.
- App `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (the STEP bore's per-platform exact triple, moves / planar feeds / arcs): the plan moved, as the pin says a planner change will. Linux x86-64 had no triple of its own (it rode the band of the other two, 16100-16260 moves); it now reads **(15561, 14837, 1561)**, two release runs identical, added as its own exact arm. Every level still verifies clean and none falls back (Z 20: 56 microlift returns, 7 rides, 1 retract hop). **The Windows (16197, 15458, 1581) and macOS (16160, 15432, 1571) triples were measured before these changes and could not be re-measured here; they are left as measured, not widened, and will fail on those platforms until re-measured there.** That re-measure is owed before this merges or at the latest at the cut (release tier).
- No golden file and no snapshot changed.

## Tests

New: `lift_swept::tests::a_rapid_landing_on_a_sub_cell_wall_strip_is_refused` (a 0.04 mm strip the cells read clear: `high` refused, allowed once the strip is cut; the hop landing's preference), `lift_swept::tests::a_disc_is_covered_on_the_cut_and_not_a_hair_past_it`, `lift_tests::a_piece_starting_where_the_tool_stands_is_ridden_on_to`.

title: feat(ui): WCS page applies its origin from the footer beside Close, and says where the origin is
body:
#870: a Makera Z1 user cut air on their first program because they hadn't understood where the origin was. Then it "took a while to find out how to actually save the setting, as the 'set origin' button is crammed next to a lot of other options".

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a.

## What changed

- **Set origin in the footer.** The WCS page's apply button leaves the page body (where it shared a row with *Level*, among the quarter turns) and moves into the property pane's fixed footer, beside *Close* (`egui_app::wcs_footer`). Every other page keeps its plain *Close*.
- **Pending edits are flagged.** While the typed X/Y/Z or angles differ from the placed WCS, the footer shows **Origin not applied** in the warning ink.
  - The position is compared to 1e-9 mm. The angles are compared as rotations, so yaw 360 is not an edit. A non-finite field reads as pending.
  - The drafts survive a close and reopen, so closing loses nothing silently. Closing does not apply them either.
- **The origin in words.** A new pure module, `app::setup_origin`, places the origin against the box the page anchors on (the stock box, else the model's bounds).
  - A point on one of the 27 anchor points is named, e.g. `top of stock, front-left corner`, `top of stock, centre` or `mid-height of stock, front edge, centred`.
  - Any other point is given as signed distances from the box's left side, front and top, so it never claims a corner it is not on.
  - The WCS page states it under its heading: `G54 origin: top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)`. The setup sheet gains an `origin:` line under the WCS numbers.
- **Viewport marker:** the WCS axis triad already marks the origin; nothing was added.
- **Docs:** `docs/user-guide/work-origin.md`, a short page on where the origin is shown and how to change it.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/870-wcs-set-origin-footer.md`.

**Overlap with #759** (@mkinney, open draft, `conflicts`): it splits the WCS page body out of `pages.rs` into `wcs_page.rs` and keeps its own *Set Origin* in the quarter-turn rows. This PR touches the page body in one place only, removing that button. The new code lives in its own files (`wcs_footer.rs`, `setup_origin.rs`). Whichever lands second drops the body button and calls `wcs_footer::origin_line` from the page.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/wcs_footer.rs` (structural: painted text, AccessKit labels, coarse placement):
  - `the_page_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words`
  - `set_origin_sits_in_the_footer_beside_close_and_nowhere_else`: one row, Set origin before Close, below the page body, exactly one apply button, no flag on a fresh page.
  - `a_typed_origin_is_flagged_until_set_origin_applies_it`: the flag appears, a click on Set origin places the typed X and clears it, and yaw 360 does not raise it.
- `app::setup_origin` unit tests: `every_anchor_point_is_named`, `a_point_off_the_anchors_is_given_as_distances_never_as_a_corner`, `a_non_finite_origin_or_box_says_so`.
- `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs`: `the_setup_sheet_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` (corner, centre, off-anchor).

Two existing ui tests got a taller window, 1280 x 900 instead of 720. The new origin line makes the WCS page one to two rows taller, and at 720 px the bottom of the page scrolls under the footer. The page scrolls; nothing is lost.
- `one_wcs::the_wcs_page_shows_the_work_offset_dropdown_and_no_setups_page_pointer`: its bottom note was out of view.
- `origin_page_shows_the_anchor_grid_and_arms_pick_mode`: its SE cell click missed.

Gates on 8b850a18:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui` (CWD `crates/ui`): all green. The lib has 596 passed and 5 ignored; every integration binary passes.

title: feat(edm): wire EDM 4-axis - upper and lower profiles paired into rulings by a stated rule
body:
Stacked on #1163 (`issue/536-wire-taper` @ b14882ea, merged into this branch first). The wire base #1139, #1144, #1147 and #1160 are merged to main; #1150 and #1158 are pending. Merge order: #1163, then this PR. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A Wire Contour can now cut the ruled surface between two profiles given separately (#290 D2).

- **Op.** `WireContourOp.four_axis: Option<WireFourAxis>` (`pairing`, `sync`, `tolerance`); absent by default, omitted from the file when absent, so a one-profile cut's file, stamp, CL and NC are unchanged. The pairing rule has no default in the file. Edited through `EditOperationParams` / the MCP parameter patch (the same JSON door); the page shows the rule, the tolerance and the sync pairs as numbers.
- **Profiles.** The selection is read as two picks (a face's one outer ring, or a closed edge chain), each flat; the higher is the upper profile. Their heights must be the op's top and bottom planes (`app::operation::wire_ruled`).
- **Pairing** (`motion::wire_edm::pairing`). One monotone map between the two rings' arc lengths, fixed by anchors: by normalised arc length from each profile's point nearest the start hole, or by sync pairs with arc length between them. A ruling at every vertex of either ring; each move ends on a ruling's lower point, its pose the wire toward the upper point; upright at the start hole. The path's note states the rule.
- **Laws** (`motion::wire_edm::ruled_laws`). Fold: consecutive rulings whose ends run against each other (`a . b < 0` - the section turns back inside the part height). Crossing: the wire's section at a quarter height crosses itself. Ruled kerf: at 33 heights the wire's section stands off the stated surface by #1163's leaning-kerf reach `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)`.
- **A twisted ruled surface.** A straight wire cannot touch it along its whole height, so offsetting both profiles by the kerf gouges between the planes (about 12 um on a square-to-round corner with a 0.33 mm kerf). The generator widens the offset on both planes, uniformly, until the kerf stands clear at every height read, says in the notes how much stands on the profile planes, and refuses past the op's `tolerance` (default 0.05 mm). A constant taper needs exactly #1163's `1 / cos(angle)`.
- **Refused by name:** crossed sync points ("sync pair #3 crosses sync pair #2"), doubled, unpaired or off-profile sync points, a folding or self-crossing pairing, open profiles or one open and one closed, a ruling past `edm.max_taper_deg` (unstated refuses), a twist past the tolerance, profiles that are not two / not flat / not on the op's planes, a taper angle stated beside the two profiles, a lead whose leaning kerf enters the surface. The U/V stroke, U/V axes, guide planes and guide reach are #1163's machine check, unchanged (it reads poses).
- **Verify.** A 4-axis cut's poses are read as the wire's lean exactly as a stated taper's; kerf, threading and slug run at every judged height; a gouge blocks the post.
- **Post.** `PARAM WireFourAxis` (the rule's words) opens the section; `wire-iso.cps` writes the same `taper_on` / `uv` / `taper_off` codes from `edm.codes` as a tapered section and names the cut in a comment.

## Sources (Clean Room)

Piegl and Tiller, "The NURBS Book" (ruled surface between two parametrised curves, chord-length parametrisation); Farin, "Curves and Surfaces for CAGD"; do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces" (the tangent plane along a ruling of a non-developable ruled surface); Liu, "Five-axis NC cylindrical milling of sculptured surfaces", CAD 27(12), 1995. No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`.

## Refresh (2026-11-13: #1163's refresh merged in, then upstream main @ a5d1a763)

- Kept both sides (also `operation/types/mod.rs` against main's `SinkerPass` export): #1163's burnout, open-run clearance and sinker fields sit beside `four_axis` in the op, DTO, job, page and every `WireContourOp` test literal.
- A 4-axis cut with a no-core burnout is refused by name (the burnout is cut vertical only), like #1163's taper + burnout refusal. Open profiles and a left/right side stay refused by the ruled generator.
- Verify still reads a 4-axis cut's poses as the wire's lean, and the leaning kerf is judged at every height. The new `burnout` flag is carried through.
- Main's posted-golden law asks a gate to judge every posted golden. `crates/app/tests/posted_gates/wire_4axis.rs` regenerates `wire_4axis_punch.cl` (byte-identical) and judges it with `taper: true` against the loft's own mesh, sliced at 25 heights: no finding, and the punch frees the part (`solid_law_goldens::the_slot_trace_and_plasma_goldens_pass_their_gates`). No law was loosened.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/wire_4axis.rs`
  - `a_square_to_round_punch_posts_its_golden_and_verifies` - goldens `tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` (a pose on every move) and `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` (synthetic fixture); the wire clause reports no problem.
  - `a_constant_taper_by_sync_points_is_the_taper_golden_and_arc_length_differs` - the CL equals #1163's `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte, the NC equals `wire_taper_punch.nc` but for the comment naming the cut; arc length on the same two profiles gives other rulings.
  - `crossed_folded_and_unpaired_sync_points_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pairing_past_the_machine_or_off_the_planes_is_refused_by_name` (max taper at generation, U stroke at the post, one profile, taper + 4-axis, planes off the profiles)
  - `a_ruling_that_gouges_the_part_blocks_the_post`
  - `the_four_axis_block_round_trips_and_its_rule_is_never_defaulted` (JSON door, stamp, undo, the door's refusal of a NaN tolerance)
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_tests.rs` (8 tests): square-to-round keeps the kerf out and a zero tolerance refuses it; arc length vs sync points; the constant taper equals `wire_contour_tapered` move for move; crossed / folded / unpaired / off-profile / doubled sync points; open and mismatched profiles; steep rulings; a conical die.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/536-wire-taper` green on the final head 263442bc (motion lib, the whole app suite set - a new golden is shared test input - and the mapped ui suites; 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## What was not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture with invented codes.
- The die side at the app level (the motion crate pins a conical die); a die whose start hole is equidistant from several sides has no single nearest point - its arc-length seam is then the first tie, and a pairing that folds or twists for it is refused, not guessed.
- A model whose tessellated twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface of its two end profiles is refused by the wire laws as a gouge (the fixtures here are split along the inner diagonal). Follow-up #1170.
- Sync points are numbers on the page, not viewport picks (#1171). Fans and profiles stitched from several runs are refused by name (#1172). Open-profile 4-axis waits for #1109.
- UI: the new rows have no structural-test assertion of their own; no snapshot PNG was changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's DTO notes are not updated (a process file); the block rides `params` through the existing tools (#1108).

Changelog: Wire EDM 4-axis: a Wire Contour cuts the ruled surface between separately picked upper and lower profiles, paired by arc length or by sync points; crossed, folding or unpaired pairings, rulings past the machine's taper and U/V limits and a twist past the stated tolerance are refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation)

title: feat(edm): wire EDM constant taper - posed moves, leaning-kerf verify, max-angle and U/V refusals
body: Stacked on #1144 (on #1139, #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Expected merges: #539 (tabs) and #540 (no-core) are worked on the same base and will likely touch `WireContourOp`, `WireParams`, the DTO and `wire_page.rs` - both sides add fields, keep both. #1147 / #1150 are stacked nearby. ## What changed A constant wire taper (#290 D2, D5, D7), as the move pose: - **Op**: `WireContourOp.taper_deg` (signed degrees; 0 = vertical, positive widens the profile downward from the top plane). The DTO omits it at 0, the stamp digests it only when non-zero, so every existing file, stamp, CL and NC is unchanged. The Geometry tab has a Taper angle field. - **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): the profile and every #532 law are held on the top plane at the kerf measured across the leaning wire (`k / cos a`). Each lower-plane vertex is moved `H tan a` along the mitre, so each side's face is planar at exactly the angle. Each move's pose is the wire's direction toward the upper guide. The wire stands upright at the start hole. Refused by name: no `edm.max_taper_deg`, an angle (or a corner's lean) above it (naming the op and the angle), a side the lean folds over, a corner too sharp to lean. - **Verify** (`sim::verify::wire`): `WireJob.taper` lifts #534's posed-move refusal only for a cut that states a taper. At every judged height the wire's section is `to + t (z - z0)`. The kerf's reach toward the product is `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)` (the leaning kerf's elliptical section). The slug is judged per height. So a gouge at any height blocks the post. - **Machine check** (`machine::wire_edm`): every pose is judged against the max taper, the guide planes (`edm.lower_guide_z` / `upper_guide_z`, which must hold the programmed plane), and the U/V offset against the U and V strokes. Missing guide planes or a missing U/V axis are refused by name. title: feat(edm): wire tabs and the tab cut-off - the slug held until it is freed, an unheld slug refused
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. Its parents (#1144, #1139, #1123, #560, #551) are merged; main merged in (open runs #1109 via PR #1147, no-core burnout #540 via PR #1160), so the diff is #539's own.

Expected merges: other open work on the same stack touches the same files additively - #538 (skim passes, on #1139) and the #1147 (open runs) integration into #1144's stack. This PR adds fields to `WireContourOp` / `WireContourDto` / `WireParams` / `WireJob` / `WireVerdict`, a new `motion::wire_edm::tabs` module and a second wire section in `posting_wire::stream`; conflicts there should be keep-both. `wire-iso.cps` is unchanged.

## What changed

Wire EDM tabs (#290 D6), off by default, and the hold law that completes #534's slug law.

- **Op parameters** (`operation::types::wire_edm`, `project::wire_edm_dto`): `tabs: { count, width, at[], cutoff_condition }` (absent = off) and `capture: bool` (absent = false). Every tab key is optional in the file, so a missing one loads and is refused by name at generation. An untabbed, uncaptured op writes no new key, so existing project files are byte-identical.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::tabs`, new): the count, width, positions and cut-off condition are each refused by name if missing. Impossible layouts are refused too: a gap (width + kerf) that does not fit on one straight side (a width at or past the side, a tab on the facets of a round), overlapping tabs, a stretch between tabs the start hole cannot reach without the kerf entering the product, and a cut-off condition whose kerf offset differs from the main cut's. The main cut leaves the tabs: each run is entered by its own lead, cut both ways, and left back along its own kerf, so the wire is never rethreaded mid-program. The cut-off follows in the same path. The path returns to the threading point once per run and once per tab, and `cutoff_split` reads the cut-off's start from that.
- **Verify** (`sim::verify::wire`): `WireJob.cutoff_from` / `capture`. For a tabbed cut, the main cut must free nothing (`TabsDoNotHold`), and the whole path must free the stated piece. An untabbed cut whose slug drops is refused (`Unsupported`) unless a capture is stated. `WireVerdict.held` / `captured` feed the report line ("holds its slug by tabs through the main cut; the tab cut-off frees ..." / "... into the stated capture").
- **Post** (`posting_wire`): a tabbed cut streams two sections. The main cut ends at a program stop (M00, so the operator secures the slug), then "<op> tab cut-off" runs with its own `EdmCondition`. The post script is not changed.
- **Stamp**: the tabs and the cut-off condition's wire and gap are digested only when tabs are on, so no existing stamp moves.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/539-wire-tabs.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_tabs.rs` (new):
  - `a_die_with_two_tabs_holds_its_slug_until_the_cut_off`: a die with two tabs. The main cut never crosses a gap, the cut-off crosses each gap once each way, the gate passes with the "held by tabs" line, and the program has the main condition, then an M00, then the cut-off condition. **New NC golden** `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_die_tabs.nc` on the synthetic fixture, with an invented second condition `C120`.
  - `an_unheld_slug_is_refused_and_a_capture_passes_it`: the same die with tabs off and no capture is refused by name ("drops unsupported"). With `capture` it passes.
  - `missing_or_impossible_tab_parameters_are_refused_by_name`: 13 refusals, each by name.
- `sim::verify::wire::hold_tests` (new): an unheld slug refused or captured; tabs hold, then the cut-off frees; a closing main cut reads "the tabs do not hold it".
- `project::wire_edm_dto::tests::the_tab_keys_round_trip_and_are_absent_when_off`.

- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/534-wire-verify`: green on dc3a06f1 (sim, motion, app, ui suites; 0 failed, 13.6 min). By hand: app `wire_tabs`, `wire_post`, `wire_verify`, `wire_contour`, `golden_cl`, `edm_machine`, `edm_conditions`; motion `--lib wire_edm`; sim `--lib wire`. Clippy `-D warnings` on motion, sim, app and ui (all targets) is clean.

title: feat(edm): sinker electrode wear compensation in Z
body:
**Stacked on #1131** (#541 sinker burn to depth, branch `issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`), which is itself stacked on #560 (#531 EDM condition table), stacked on #551 (#530 EDM machine kinds). The chain is #551 -> #560 -> #1131 -> this PR. Until those merge, their commits show here; this PR adds one commit on top of #1131's head. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **A wear rate per condition.** `edm.conditions[]` gains an optional `wear`: the electrode's axial wear rate, as mm of electrode lost per mm burned (dimensionless, not unit-scaled). `parse_mch` (so `LoadMachine` and the project reader) and `Edm::is_sane` refuse a rate that is not a finite ratio in [0, 1), by name ("... is not an axial wear rate ..."). No rate ships with any machine; rates are user data (#290 D4).
- **A measured wear and a layer step on the op.** `SinkerBurnOp` gains `layer`, `wear_lost` and `wear_over`. A wear measured between burns (length lost over depth burned) wins over the condition's rate. With neither stated, the burn is **not compensated**: the path note and the op page say `electrode wear: not compensated (no wear rate stated)`. `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` (and the project reader) refuse a measured rate of 1 or more, a half-stated or non-finite measurement, and a non-positive layer step, all by name, through a new `OpParams::named_refusal` door that runs ahead of the generic "not usable".
- **Compensation in Z** (`crates/motion/src/sinker_wear.rs`, `burn_compensated`). The burn is fed in layers. Each layer's tip is programmed `rate * d` deeper, where `d` is how far that layer's nominal floor lies below the work top. Every move is re-checked against the bound: the stated floor plus the gap, minus `rate` times the stated depth. A move past it is refused as over-deep, by name. All of #541's refusals still apply. The electrode-length law now reads the deeper, compensated tip. With no rate and no layer step, the moves are exactly #541's (pinned).
- **The stock sim judges the worn electrode.** `plan_program` maps each programmed tip back to where the worn electrode burns (`worn_tip`, the exact inverse of the compensation). A compensated burn to the cavity's own floor therefore reads 0 gouge cells, and a nominal floor past the model is still convicted.
- **Staleness.** The op digest adds the layer step and the measured wear, and the stamp adds the condition's rate, each only when stated. Existing digests do not change.
- **File, MCP, UI.** The three op keys are additive and optional: older files load unchanged and write no new keys. MCP drives them through the existing params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation`). No new command or tool was needed, and a test pins this. The Sinker Burn page's Passes tab gains Layer step, Measured wear and Measured over, plus the compensation status line.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/546-sinker-wear-comp.md`.

## How tested
- New suite `crates/app/tests/sinker_wear.rs`:
  - `sinker_wear_layers_match_golden`: golden `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_wear_layers.cl`. I read it: three 2 mm layers at rate 0.02, gap 0.05, with tips at Z 18.010, 15.970 and 13.930 (that is 18.05 - 0.04, 16.05 - 0.08 and 14.05 - 0.12).
  - `a_condition_wear_rate_deepens_each_layer_and_the_sim_judges_it_clean`
  - `a_missing_wear_rate_shows_not_compensated`
  - `a_bad_wear_rate_is_refused_by_name`: machine file and op commands.
  - `a_measured_wear_wins_over_the_condition_and_round_trips_the_file`: includes an older file with no new keys.
  - `the_wear_fields_ride_the_mcp_params_door`
- Unit tests in `motion::sinker_wear`: wear off equals the plain burn, per-layer deepening plus its inverse, and refusals of the rate, step and reach.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn.rs`: the op literal gains the three new `None` fields; no assertion changed.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on this head (b0e121ce), 24.3 min. The tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites pass. In the app suites, every binary passes except one test, and that test **fails on #1131's own head too**: I ran it alone on `origin/issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`, and this PR doesn't change it:
  - `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`: "SinkerBurn is judged while a tolerance is left". The fidelity law refuses a Sinker Burn on a reduced-fidelity model, but the test expects it to be judged.
  The fix belongs on #1131. The sinker_burn, sinker_wear, edm_machine, edm_conditions, golden_cl and project_roundtrip suites pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **Not exercised on a real EDM control** (#290 D10). The conditions and wear rates are synthetic fixtures.
- Wear is axial only; corner and side wear are not modelled. No orbit (#544), no multi-electrode undersize logic (#543), and no sinker post (#542). Layers are a stepped plunge with no retract between them.
- The field-arm stock view still refuses an electrode program (as in #541).

Changelog: Sinker EDM: electrode wear compensation in Z - a stated axial wear rate (per condition in the machine file, or measured on the op) deepens each burn layer by the wear it states, bounded and refused by name past it; with no rate the burn says "not compensated" (#546)

See docs/decisions/546-sinker-wear-comp.md ("merge with orbit and side burn").

title: feat(sinker): generate an electrode from a cavity's picked faces
body:
Stacked on #1136 (→ #1131 → #560 → #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Until those merge, this PR's diff against `main` includes theirs; its own change is the last commit.

## What changed

A sinker EDM electrode is generated from the picked faces of a part's cavity - its level floor and every vertical wall standing on it - and added to the document as #541's electrode tool, in one undo step.

- **`motion::sinker_cavity::cavity_of`** (pure, no world) reads a face set as one cavity. Each face is checked on its own (finite, in range, planar, non-zero area, closed boundary), classed by its outward normal, and the walls are matched to the floor's outer ring edge by edge: a wall stands on a floor edge when one of its edges lies on it at floor height and its normal points into the floor. Every floor edge must be covered end to end.
- **`motion::sinker_electrode::derive`** offsets the outline inward by `undersize + orbit` with the geometry crate's polygon offset (`geo2d::Region::offset_sharp`, Clipper2) and extends the electrode a stated stub above the cavity's mouth. The sizes are the arithmetic `cavity - 2 x inset`; the offset polygon must agree within 10 nm or the derivation refuses.
- **`standing_in`** clips the part's facets against the cavity's column above the floor: a boss, a rib or an overhang in the electrode's way refuses the electrode with the spot.
- **`operation::sinker_faces`** resolves the picks (the one pick rule, #692; outward normals by the facets' winding) and reads a condition's undersize by id through #531's door.
- **`commands::ElectrodeFromFaces`** is the undoable command (its write and inverse are `AddTool`'s). **MCP: `electrode_from_faces`** runs it; its reply carries a `burn` object that `add_operation`'s `params` takes as is.

## Rectangular cavities only, for now

The stock sim burns an electrode with #541's box atom: an axis-aligned rectangular face. So only a cavity whose outline is an axis-aligned rectangle yields an electrode. A rounded corner, a rotated rectangle, an L, a curved wall, a drafted wall or a stepped floor is refused by name, and the refusal names the follow-up: **#1152** (a sim atom and a tool record for an electrode body). The offset outline is already computed and carried on the result for it.

Orbit (#544) is not merged: an optional orbit radius is accepted and taken off the electrode, and the tool's answer says so. Until #544 changes #543's size law, a Sinker Burn judges such an electrode without its orbit.

## Refusals, each by name

Empty face set · a face with a non-finite or out-of-range coordinate · a zero-area or degenerate face · an open loop (a boundary that does not close) · a curved (welded) or non-planar wall · a leaning (drafted) wall or tilted floor · a face looking down · no floor · two floors (faces from different cavities, or a stepped cavity) · only the floor · a wall of another cavity (stands on none of the floor's edges, reaches below it, or faces away) · walls that do not close around the floor · a self-intersecting outline · a non-rectangular cavity (#1152) · an inset that consumes the cavity · a garbled undersize, orbit, stub or pickup · picks on different models, on no part, a stale id, a chain or a vertex · an open, inside-out or non-manifold body · the part standing in the cavity's column · a taken or reserved tool name.

## How tested

Run one by one (`cargo test -p <crate> ... -- --exact` style), debug:

- `camcraft-motion --lib sinker_electrode` (7 tests): `a_rectangular_cavitys_faces_yield_its_electrode`, `a_cavity_reads_whatever_the_winding_split_or_order`, `every_degenerate_face_set_is_refused_by_its_own_name`, `a_cavity_the_box_atom_cannot_burn_is_refused_by_name`, `the_model_standing_in_the_cavitys_column_is_found`, and the seeded fuzz: `fuzz_a_damaged_cavity_is_always_refused_by_name_never_a_panic` (6000 sound cavities, each then damaged one of 20 named ways and required to refuse by that name) and `fuzz_garbage_faces_never_panic_and_never_answer_a_nonsense_electrode` (20000 garbage face sets with NaN, infinities, `f64::MAX`, denormals).
- `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode` (8 tests): `a_pockets_faces_yield_an_electrode_that_burns_that_pocket_in_the_sim` (the generated rough leaves stock and gouges nothing, the generated finish leaves the program verdict clean), `the_verdict_convicts_the_generated_electrode_burned_off_its_point` (the contrast: 1 mm off centre gouges), `the_electrode_is_one_undo_step_and_its_name_is_checked`, `the_condition_door_reads_the_undersize_or_refuses_by_name`, `a_face_set_that_is_no_single_cavity_is_refused_by_name`, `faces_from_different_cavities_are_refused_by_name`, `a_boss_in_the_cavity_is_in_the_electrodes_way`, `a_rounded_pocket_is_refused_by_name_until_the_sim_burns_a_body`.
- `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode_mcp`: `the_electrode_is_generated_and_burned_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands`.

The fuzz found one hole while this was written: a denormal stub vanished into the depth, giving an electrode no longer than its cavity. The stub now has a floor (1 micron) and the length is checked against the depth.

Gate (local, debug, head `c93678aa`):
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib`: 205 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode --test sinker_electrode_mcp --test sinker_burn --test sinker_undersize --test mcp --test mcp_pick --test mcp_pockets --test mcp_order --test commands_undo --test tool_law --test pocket_recognition --test edm_conditions --test edm_machine`: 109 passed, 0 failed.

## What was not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** Synthetic conditions and parts built in code only (#290 D10).

title: feat(edm): Wire Contour skim passes - per-pass condition, offset and direction
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Expected merges: retarget to `main` after #1139 merges. #1143 (Wire UI, also on #1139) touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs`; this PR changes one line there (the op destructure gains `..`), so a trivial conflict at most. #534 (verify) and #1109 (open profile) on #1123 are not touched.

## What changed

The Wire Contour gains skim passes: a rough pass, then N skims, each naming its own machine condition (and so its own offset, wire radius + that condition's gap), with an optional direction reversal per skim.

- `operation::WireContourOp.skims: Vec<WireSkim { condition, reverse }>`; file / MCP JSON `skims: [{ condition, reverse? }]`, absent when empty (rough-only files and goldens unchanged). Edits ride `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the existing MCP params door.
- Command door (`wire_op::condition_of`): every skim's condition resolved through #531's door, refused by name when it names none or the machine does not state it; then `motion::wire_edm::check_passes`: a pass nearer the profile than the finishing (last) pass ("would cut past the finished profile", rough included), a skim farther out than the pass before it ("would cut only air"), a skim condition with another wire diameter ("one threading cuts every pass with one wire").
- Generator: `motion::wire_edm::wire_passes` (new `skims.rs`) runs #532's single-pass generator per pass at its own offset, every law at that offset; each pass leads in from the threading point and back; a reversed skim walks clockwise. No skims is `wire_contour` exactly.
- Stamp digests each skim's condition numbers and direction (writes nothing for no skims - no stored stamp moves).
- Post stream (`posting_wire`): a mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition <skim id>` before each skim's first move (after each return to the threading point); a path that does not return once per pass is refused.
- `wire-iso.cps`: a condition that arrives with the wire threaded is the next skim's - `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `comp_off` again at its first move; the wire stays threaded.
- **Wire laws (#534) and skims** (merge with main, 2026-11-13): `sim::verify::wire` now judges each move at its own pass's kerf. Before this, every move was judged at the rough's kerf, which read skim 1 as a false 0.0200 mm gouge at move 8 (0.165 - 0.145). `WireJob.skim_offsets`, new `passes.rs`: the path is split at each return to the threading point, the threading law takes the widest pass, and the slug law sweeps each pass at its own offset. Skims on an open run are refused at the door and in the law. The arithmetic is in the decision record.

title: feat(edm): wire contour cuts an open run from the stock's edge
body:
Stacked on #1144 (on #1139, #1123, #560, #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560, #1123, #1139, #1144 first. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The Wire Contour op (#532) now cuts **one open run entered from the stock's edge** - a cut-off line, a slot, a relief - besides one closed profile (part of #290).

- **Kerf side stated, never inferred:** `side` gains `left` / `right` (of the run's travel = its point order) beside `die` / `punch`. Die/punch on an open run is refused by name ("an open profile has no punch or die side; state the kerf side: left or right of the run's travel"); left/right on a closed profile likewise. Still no serde default for `side`.
- **No start hole:** both ends must reach (or pass) the stock's edge (1 um tolerance). The path is the run's one-sided parallel at wire radius + gap (mitred joins), extended along the run's own end directions until the wire stands **kerf offset + a stated `clearance`** off the stock: threaded there in the air, run out the same way at the far end (no return).
- **Refused by name:** no stock, an end that stops inside the stock (with its distance), a run that never enters the stock, a self-crossing run, one that doubles back, several runs or a run mixed with rings, an inside corner tighter than wire radius + gap (cover law, same 2 um as #532), a run-out that would cut the stock, a bad clearance.
- The kerf law and the cover law now run over an open polyline too (`laws::cover_run`, `kerf(.., given_closed, ..)`); the closed path is byte-identical (both #532 goldens unchanged).
- App: `WireContourOp.clearance` (seeded 1.0 mm; the file omits it at the seed, so closed-cut files read/write as before), `is_sane` bounds it, the generator gets the setup's stock outline (stock facets projected to XY, read only when a run is picked). The existing MCP door (`params_from_json` / the edit patch) carries `side: left|right` and `clearance` - no new MCP tool (#1108 is the dedicated one).
- UI: the minimal wire page offers the four sides and a "Run-out clearance" row (#535 owns the real page).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1109-wire-open-profile.md` (side in one field, travel = point order, no centred kerf yet, no blind runs - a run ending inside the material is a closed cut from a start hole, run-out shape, clearance seed).

## Readings

Plate 100 x 50, synthetic condition C110 (wire 0.25, gap 0.04, offset 0.165), clearance 1.0. Cut-off at x = 60, kerf right: every wire point at x = 60.165 (1e-9); threaded at Y-1.165, run out at Y51.165. Left: x = 59.835 - the two stand apart by the 0.33 kerf. A U slot from the edge (2 mm corners, kerf left, inside the U): every ride point exactly 0.165 off the run (1e-6) and inside the slot; the same U with sharp corners is refused ("minimum inside radius is 0.1650 mm") on the left and cut (mitred) on the right.

## Integration with #1144 (wire-iso post #1139 + wire verify #534)

`issue/534-wire-verify` is merged into this branch (`5c49075a`, no textual conflicts) and the open run is joined to both (`0d82d2e7`):

- **Verify** (`sim::verify::wire`): a third side `CutSide::Open` for `left|right`. The kerf law judges the run, run-in and run-out included, against the part at every judged height, so an open run whose kerf touches the part is a gouge and blocks the post. The start-hole/threading and slug laws are skipped, and the report line says so: "Cutoff1 open run (right of travel): kerf judged; start-hole and slug laws not applied (...)". Both ends, where the wire is threaded and cut, must stand clear of the stock by the kerf offset at every height (`OpenEndInStock`). The app gate maps `left|right` to `Open` and no longer refuses an open run for having no start hole.
- **Post** (`wire-iso.cps`): it threads at the path's first point (the run-in, in the air) and cuts the wire at section end after the run-out. It writes only the path's moves, so no return to the threading point exists. Without AWT the operator notes read "at the run-in point outside the stock" and "at the run-out point". The closed punch golden is byte-identical.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1109-wire-open-profile.md` now covers how verify and the post read an open run.

## How tested

- `camcraft-motion` lib `wire_edm::open_tests` (3): `a_cut_off_across_a_plate_stands_the_kerf_offset_on_the_stated_side`, `a_slot_from_the_edge_rides_inside_at_the_kerf_offset`, `every_open_run_refusal_is_named`; #532's 5 `wire_edm::tests` unchanged and green.
- `golden_cl`: new `wire_open_cutoff_matches_golden` (`tests/golden/wire_open_cutoff.cl`); `wire_contour_die_and_punch_match_golden` unchanged - **no golden moved**.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_contour`: new `the_open_run_fields_ride_the_commands_and_the_json_door` (EditOperationParams + undo, NaN clearance refused at the door, JSON door both ways, a closed file names no clearance, left/right on the closed slug refused at generation).
- Integration: `wire_post::an_open_cutoff_posts_its_golden_and_a_gouging_one_is_refused` (new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_open_cutoff.nc`, synthetic fixture dialect). A 60x50x12 part in a 100x50x12 bar, its x=60 top edge picked as an open chain: it generates through the commands, is judged, and posts with one G0 to the run-in at Y-1.165, cuts to Y51.165, then FX-CUT with no return. The same run with its kerf on the part's side is refused at the post (`Cutoff1: wire gouge`) and no NC is written. The punch golden is asserted byte-identical. Also `sim` `verify::wire::tests::an_open_run_is_judged_by_its_kerf_with_no_start_hole_or_slug` (clean pass with no slug and the skip said; a gouge; an end in the stock).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/534-wire-verify` on the final head `0d82d2e7`: **green**, 13.7 min (sim 3 s, motion lib 27 s, app 676 s: every suite because a shared golden changed, wire_post/wire_contour/wire_verify included; ui 115 s). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
