title: feat(sim): wire EDM 2.5D verification - kerf, threading and slug laws block the post
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560, #1123, #1139 first. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Not exercised on a real EDM control.

**Integration with #1139 (#533 wire post).** `issue/533-wire-iso-post` is merged into this branch (`8cd0aff6`), keeping both sides: `posting_wire.rs` holds #533's Wire Contour stream and this PR's wire clause, mounted once in `posting.rs` as `wire` with the clause re-exported; `wire_contour.rs` asserts the combined truth (the note points at the wire laws, and the wire cut streams with its condition). With a real wire post underneath, the verdict now stands between a judged cut and NC text: `wire_post::the_wire_laws_stand_between_the_cut_and_its_nc_text` (`3e852d68`) posts the clean punch through `wire-iso.cps` to #533's golden (unchanged, byte-identical) and refuses a die whose kerf burns the plate by name (`Die1: wire gouge: the kerf of move ...`), writing no NC file.

## What changed

Wire EDM verification of a 2-axis cut (#534, part of #290 D7). Every finding blocks the post; nothing is a warning.

**Laws** - `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/` (pure 2D, `judge(&WireJob) -> WireVerdict`):
- **Kerf law (gouge).** Each move's segment must stay at least the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap, from the condition) from the product's section, and must not stand in it, at every judged height. The first move that breaks it is named with its depth, the spot, the height and how many moves gouge. The check uses exact point-to-segment distance, not an area threshold.
- **Threading law.** The start hole must be stated, the path must start at it, and the product must stand clear of it by the kerf offset at every height through the full stock height. Each failure is refused by name.
- **Slug law.** The kerf (the offset disc swept along the whole path, `Region::sweep`) is taken out of the material section (stock and part), and the connected pieces inside the cut's filled outline are the ones freed. A die whose freed piece holds part material ("the part drops") is refused, and so is a punch whose freed pieces hold none ("only waste drops"). A cut that frees nothing is refused too.
- **What "the part" is, by the stated side.** For a punch it is the model. For a die it is the model when the start hole stands outside it (a die plate with the opening as its hole). When the start hole stands inside the model, the model is the opening (#532's whole-model die) and the stock around it is the product.

**Gate** - `crates/app`:
- `operation/wire_verify.rs` gathers the inputs live, at the post. That is the cached path, the condition's offset, the side and start, and the part and stock sliced at both ends of the span the wire passes plus about every 2 mm between (at most 9 heights). The span covers the op's planes, the part and the stock, whichever reaches farthest.
- `posting_wire.rs` adds the wire clause to `verification_report`, beside the plasma clause. Every finding is a blocking problem. The not-judged line says the 3D stock sim did not run for the wire, and names the piece each cut frees: "Die1 frees 7xx mm² near X0 Y0 (waste)" or "Punch1 frees ... (the part)".
- A wire cut taken from the stock, or one with no path, is refused by name at the gate.
- The machine check's wire note no longer says verification is not built. It now points to the post's wire laws, and the one assertion in `wire_contour.rs` that read the old note was updated to match.

Decisions in `docs/decisions/534-wire-verify.md`. They cover: judged live at the post, the whole height the wire passes, exact distance rather than area, the product reading per side, threading clearance = the kerf offset, slug connectivity, and no capture/tab law until #539.

## How tested

- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::wire::tests` (5): `a_correct_punch_passes_and_drops_the_punch`, `a_correct_die_passes_whether_the_model_is_the_opening_or_the_plate`, `a_kerf_into_the_part_is_a_gouge_naming_the_move`, `a_missing_moved_or_crowded_start_hole_is_refused`, `the_slug_is_read_for_the_stated_side` (a punch stated on a die plate's hole, a die stated on a punch outline, and a die plate with no stock).
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify` (3), through the commands and the gate: `a_correct_die_and_a_correct_punch_pass_and_name_the_piece_they_free`, `a_kerf_into_the_part_blocks_the_post_naming_the_move` (a 12 mm opening model in a 20 mm plate, so above the opening the wire burns the plate), `a_missing_start_hole_blocks_the_post`.
- `wire_contour` (7) still green, with the machine note's assertion updated.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/issue/532-wire-contour` on the final head `82bf9b54`: **green**, 4 steps and 0 failed (sim 19 s, motion 9 s, app 602 s for the whole suite list including `wire_contour` and `wire_verify`, ui 90 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- After merging #1139: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head `3e852d68`: **green**, 4 steps, 0 failed (sim 12 s, motion 4 s, app 522 s incl. `wire_post` 5, `wire_contour` 7, `wire_verify` 3, ui 86 s); clippy -D warnings on sim/app clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The condition is synthetic, and nothing was cut.
- On this PR alone (without #1139) there is no wire post; the integration above is what puts the verdict in front of NC text.
- Taper (#536): the laws read straight, vertical, unposed moves and refuse anything else by name. The ruled surface between planes is not judged.
- Capture/tabs (#539, D6): a correct slug passes and is named on the report line. An unsupported slug is not refused, because no capture parameter exists yet.
- A pre-drilled start hole's diameter is not modelled (the op states a point). "Too small" means the product stands within the kerf offset of the threading point.
- Only the op's source model is judged. Another model on the same setup that stands in the wire's column is not checked.
- A selection-sourced (picked-edge) wire cut was not tested through the gate.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour is verified at the post in 2.5D: a kerf into the part (naming the move), a missing or crowded start hole, and a slug on the wrong side (die vs punch) or a cut that frees nothing each block the post by name, and the report names the piece each cut frees (#534)

title: feat(edm): generic ISO-style sinker post, every EDM code from the machine's edm.codes
body:
Branch carries upstream/main a9ec0982 (merged twice, no rebase; it trial-merges clean with 683802be, a verify-only change). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Reworked onto main's EDM designs (wire post #533, serves law #1232/#1266); decisions in `docs/decisions/542-sinker-iso-post.md` under "2026-11-12 - rework onto main's EDM designs".

## What changed
- **`assets/posts/sinker-iso.cps`** ("Sinker EDM (ISO)", `posting::SINKER_POSTS`): a generic ISO-style sinker post. It writes the RS-274 words itself (G0 with changed axis words, G90, the setup's work offset, `( )` comments) and takes every EDM-specific code from the machine's `edm.codes` (#290 D5): `metric` / `inch`, `pickup` (`{tool}`), `reference` (`{offset}`), `condition` (`{id}`), `depth` (`{z}`, optional `{f}`), `end`. A missing code, a placeholder the post does not fill, or one with no value is refused by name. A burn posts as rapid approach, the `depth` code, rapid retract; a feed with X/Y travel, a feed up, an arc, a cycle, compensation, an rpm or a coolant ask is refused by name.
- **Refused by name, never posted silently wrong (new in the rework):** a condition the machine's `edm.conditions` does not list (exact id, as the table writes it); an orbit (#544 - its explicit moves are what the stock sim judged, never swapped for the control's orbit word, even a listed one); a Sinker Side Burn (#545).
- **Codes: main's store and validator.** Main's `Machine.edm_codes` and `post::machine::edm_codes` (lowercase names, printable text, `CODE_MAX`, no brackets). The PR's own `Edm.codes` store and looser parser are dropped; `SINKER_CODES` stays as the list of names the sinker post reads, pinned to pass main's law.
- **serves: main's manifest and door.** `serves = ["sinker_edm"];` and the registry (`BUILTINS`, `SINKER_POSTS`, `post_serves`, `default_post_for`, `post_offer`) beside main's wire entries. The PR's engine `serves_gate` is dropped. Main's `posting_family::edm_at_post` ("no post for a sinker EDM machine yet (#542)") is retired: every writer's `posting_serves::refusal` right after it refuses any post that does not serve a sinker, by name.
- **`PARAM SinkerCondition`** (was `EdmCondition` in this PR): main's `EdmCondition` is the wire section's word and main's engine refuses it through any script without `wireEdm`. The sinker gets its own word and an engine door beside the wire one: `SinkerCondition` through a script whose `serves` does not name `sinker_edm` is refused by name. The wire door is unchanged.
- **Stream PARAMs** (`crates/app/src/posting_edm.rs`): `SinkerCondition`, `ElectrodePickup` for a Sinker Burn and a Sinker Side Burn; `EdmOrbit` / `EdmOrbitRadius` for an orbit.

title: feat(thread): external threads on a boss at the operation level
body:
Stack order: #1005 (`issue/894-thread-mill`) -> #1045 (`issue/992-thread-undrilled`) -> this PR. #1005 and #1045 have merged to main (f0c316ff, 07cb331f); this PR now stands on main alone (merged at 36035af8). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The Thread operation cuts external threads on a boss.

- **`external` on the operation.** `OpParams::Thread { external }`: the list then holds bosses (`radius` = major radius, `entry_z` = top, `floor_z` = shoulder). File / MCP key `external`, additive, written only when set; the stamp digests it only when set, so no internal thread goes Stale.
- **Boss recognition.** `drilling::recognize_bosses`: the hole recogniser's weld, circle fit and rim-span law with the facing vote inverted (closed round upright walls facing away from their axis). Stepped walls are never folded. Detect holes (button and MCP `detect_holes`) reads bosses when the operation is external. The Thread page gets "External thread (on a boss)", "Detect bosses" and a per-row Remove (a round base is a boss too).
- **Judging a tool beside a boss, without the silhouette** (`operation::thread_boss`):
  - crest law: tangency against each boss's MINOR circle (major less 0.6134 x pitch), nothing else in the region. The drawn wall is not what the crests answer to, so a matched thread is not convicted on every helix (the #1071 flaw, not repeated);
  - root law: the solid law with the cutter narrowed by the EXTERNAL depth (`thread_op::root_cutter`, external threads only): roots, tip, shank, holder against the whole part, shoulder included. A boss gets no bore grant (`thread_op::bores` is empty for it), so the grant and a narrowed cutter are never stacked; internal threads use #1005's #1071 laws (`major_rims` + the thread grant) unchanged;
  - neighbour law (new): the crest ring at full radius over the cutting length against every facet that is not the threaded boss's own wall, gouge tolerance only. The boss a run of feeds threads is read from the helix's own centre, never from nearness.
- **Air law** (`thread_entry::judge_bosses`, #992's external analogue): every position the feeds take the tool through is read in the stock the program ahead leaves; a column under the tool's disc, more than one cell outside the boss, standing above the tip refuses the thread by name (place, heights, how far out and how deep to clear). Unknown prior is refused.
- **Round-boss law** (`thread_boss::not_round`): a boss whose wall is not a tessellated circle (a hex stud, a square post) is refused at generate by name - "the boss at (x, y) is not round - external thread milling needs a round boss". The crest law and the neighbour law both take the boss wall for a circle, so a polygon's flats would be cut unjudged. Same sagitta test as the internal side's `walls_round` (`verify::hole_is_round`), on the boss wall.
- **Door** (create / edit / retool, again at generate): a boss no thicker than the thread is deep; a thread longer than the mill reaches beside a boss (shank wider than the tooth roots, or the holder); infeed against the external depth.
- **Simulation.** An external thread is swept at its external root radius (`thread_op::sim_radius`); the internal depth read 0.07 x pitch of the boss as cut and the post gate called it a gouge. Internal threads and taps unchanged.
- The kernel ride is used as #1005 pinned it; nothing in #1005 / #1045 was reworked. No bugs found in them.

## Sources

ISO 68-1 / ISO 965-1 / DIN 13 (external design root 17/24 H = 0.6134 P); Machinery's Handbook, "Thread milling"; Smid, "CNC Programming Handbook", thread milling chapter; Sutherland-Hodgman clipping and point-to-polygon distance (O'Rourke). No HSMWorks / Fusion material consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/985-external-threads.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/thread_boss.rs` (12 tests): `a_hex_stud_is_no_round_boss_and_is_refused_by_name`, `an_external_m8_thread_verifies_clean_and_posts_helical_moves` (generator verdict, post gate and program sim clean; G02 with Z; goldens), `a_single_form_mill_threads_an_m10_boss_one_turn_per_thread`, `left_hand_and_conventional_external_threads_verify_clean_too`, `detect_reads_the_bosses_of_an_external_thread_and_holes_of_an_internal_one`, `a_boss_standing_in_uncut_stock_is_refused_by_name`, `a_part_wall_the_roughing_left_standing_in_the_sweep_is_refused`, `a_wall_inside_the_crest_rings_sweep_is_a_gouge_that_blocks_the_post`, `impossible_bosses_are_refused_when_the_operation_is_made`, `a_hole_list_read_as_bosses_never_passes_silently`, `moving_the_roughing_after_the_thread_marks_it_stale_and_refuses_it`, `the_external_flag_edits_undoes_and_round_trips_the_project_file`.
- Unit: `operation::thread_boss::tests` (7), `operation::thread_entry::tests` (3 new), `operation::thread_op::tests::an_external_thread_narrows_the_roots_by_the_external_depth`, `drilling::boss::tests` (4).
- MCP: `mcp::external_thread_milling_over_the_tools`. UI: `thread_mill_page_tests::the_geometry_tab_switches_between_holes_and_bosses_and_apply_undoes`, `a_listed_feature_can_be_removed_from_the_draft`.
- Goldens: `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.cl`, `nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc`, `thread_mill_external_m10_single_form.cl`.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 29e097c9 (refreshed #1045 @ 6dd3f773 + main @ 683802be: tools 4s, sim 21s, motion 155s, app 842s, ui 30s; 17.6 min, 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Thread suites run one by one: thread_mill 8, thread_mill_rim 11, thread_boss 12, thread_entry 5, hole_wall_flats 5, solid_law_goldens 7 (posted_gates/thread), coarse_rims 5, lib `thread` 18, mcp thread/fill_openings 3 - all green. Final head 4f15b9b3 adds only a clean merge of main @ 36035af8 (MCP tools, #1005/#1045 merges); thread suites and the mcp suite re-run green on it, clippy app+ui clean.

## Not exercised / left open

- A polygonal boss (hex stud, square post) is refused, not threaded; threading over flats is left for a follow-up if asked for.
- No viewport pick of a boss: recognition plus Remove only. Follow-up #1132.
- A near-net or cast stock with nothing machined ahead is refused (as a cored hole is under #992). Posed (3+2) external threads are refused.
- The simulation does not draw the thread form; the boss shows at its drawn diameter.
- The neighbour law walks the facets the path's box reaches with no spatial index; not timed on a large model.
- No real machine run; NC checked by the golden and the Fanuc post only.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs` (already over 400 lines) grew by one test; the camcraft-mcp skill text is not updated (process file).
- MCP: covered by the existing `add_operation` / `edit_operation` / `detect_holes` tools; no new tool.

Changelog: Thread milling cuts external threads on a boss: an External option with boss detection, refusals by name for a boss too thin, a thread past the mill's reach and stock left standing around the boss (#985)
Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #985

title: feat(edm): sinker rough and finish with undersize from their conditions
body:
Stacked on #1131 (→ #560 → #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **Sinker Burn passes** (sibling ops, one electrode per op): each Sinker Burn gains `pass` (single / rough / finish; single keeps #541's law unchanged) and the finished cavity `cavity_x` / `cavity_y`.
- **Undersize law** (`motion::sinker_undersize::judge`): a rough or finish reads its condition's `undersize` and `gap` through #531's `Edm::condition` by id, after the sinker-kind check (`sinker_op::condition`, the door the gap and undersize now share). Per axis it refuses by name: electrode + 2×gap wider than the cavity (the wall would be burned past size), a finish that burns short of the cavity ("sinker finish leaves the cavity under size"), and an electrode that is not `cavity - 2×undersize`. The tip stands one undersize above the finished floor (`SinkerParams.stand`), so a rough leaves `undersize - gap` on floor and walls alike.
- **Order law**: a finish looks back (program order, same setup, unsuppressed) for the rough of the same cavity. If its undersize is not smaller, a new advisory `Warning::SinkerFinishOrder` names both numbers. It does not hold the post, because the finish's own size law already holds the cavity to size.
- Stamp digests the undersize and the rough a finish follows. DTO keys are additive and written only for rough or finish. The UI Passes tab gains the pass and the cavity X/Y.

title: feat(post): Fanuc Lathe writes inch programs from the document's unit
body:
Stacked on #981 (on #961). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` now writes an inch document as an inch program instead of refusing it. It declares `programUnits = "mm inch"` and reads `postOptions.Units`. The stream and every geometry or refusal check stay in mm; values are converted only in the word formatters:

| Word | G21 (unchanged) | G20 (new) |
|---|---|---|
| X (diameter), Z, I K, G76 first-block R, tool note D/R | mm, 3 dp | in, 4 dp |
| G99 F (feed per rev) | mm/rev, 4 dp | in/rev, 4 dp |
| G32 / G76 F (lead) | mm, 4 dp | in, 6 dp |
| G76 P(k) Q(dmin) Q(1st), G83 Q (no-point increments) | whole microns | whole 0.0001 in |
| G96 S | m/min | ft/min (m/min / 0.3048) |
| G97 S, G50 S, G83 P dwell, G76 P(m)(r)(a) | unchanged | unchanged |
| PART LOAD advance comment | `ADVANCE 30` | `ADVANCE 1.1811 IN` |

**Refused by name, never guessed:**
- A C-axis live-tool section on an inch program. Its feed is a composite rate that counts degrees as the linear unit, and how that rate works under G20 was not confirmed from a public source.
- A per-rev feed that rounds to `F0` at the program's digits.
- A G76 depth smaller than one least increment.

`program_units` drops Fanuc Lathe from its mm-only list, and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` says the same. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/977-fanuc-lathe-inch.md`.

## Sources (public, behaviour only)
- RS-274 / ISO 6983 for G20 / G21.
- The public Fanuc 0i-T lathe programming vocabulary the post was already specced from: G96 / G97 / G50, G99, and the two-block G76 with P / Q as no-point counts of the least input increment (0.001 mm, or 0.0001 in under inch input).
- Published lathe programming guides with inch two-line G76 examples that use four-digit P / Q in 0.0001 in.

No vendor post, Fusion or HSMWorks material was used.

## How tested
- New suite `lathe_post_inch` (fixtures in `tests/fanuc_lathe_inch/`):
  - `every_turning_stream_posts_the_mm_program_in_inches`: covers facing, profile rough + finish, groove + part, axial drill, the G76 thread and the G32 thread. Each mm post must match its committed mm golden byte for byte, and Units mm must post exactly what no unit posts. Each inch program is checked word by word against its mm twin (lengths / 25.4, feeds / 25.4, increments / 2.54, SFM = m/min x 3.28084, everything else equal, G20 before any motion, no G21). The inch programs are committed under `golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/`.
  - `the_inch_thread_words_are_pinned`: `G76 P010000 Q157 R0` / `G76 X0.378 Z0.315 P472 Q157 F0.07874`, plus the G32 lead `F0.07874`.
  - `an_inch_document_posts_inch_through_the_gate`: SetUnits inch, then `post_setup` gives the same program as the engine.
  - `surface_speed_is_feet_per_minute_and_rpm_never_scales`: `G96 S656` from 200 m/min, with `G50 S12000` unchanged.
  - `a_peck_counts_the_inch_increment`: `G83 ... Q394 P500`.
  - `what_inch_cannot_say_soundly_is_refused_by_name`.
- I also ran these suites by hand, all green: lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, program_units, mcp_units, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, lathe_post_tormach, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_blade_corner, lathe_nose_tip, coolant_followups, comment_escape, conformance, inverted_post, control_comp, wear_comp, program_entry, and every turning* suite.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/902-document-units` (the new golden dir makes it run every app suite): green on 8e26be0c (all app suites, 12.9 min); clippy `-D warnings` clean on the new suite and program_units.
- No existing golden moved.

## Not exercised
- No real control. The inch digits (4 dp lengths and per-rev feeds, 6 dp leads, 0.0001 in increments) follow the published inch least increment and have not been proved on a 0i-T.
- Rounding per-rev feeds to 4 dp in inch is coarse on very small feeds: 0.0267 mm/rev posts as F0.001, about 5% low. That is a slower cut, never a faster one; see the decision file.
- C-axis live tooling in inch is refused, not converted.

## #931 slice 3 of 3: the Setups combo lists the post's offsets; MCP takes an index

**Stacked on #1113 → #1101 → #945.** This PR targets `main`, so until those merge its diff also shows their commits. This slice is only the top two commits (`feat(ui,mcp): ...` and `fix(ui): ...`). Merge order: #945, #1101, #1113, then this one, retargeting each child before its parent merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Effort: high (no escalation).

### What changed
- **Setups page / WCS page combo** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_pick.rs`): lists offsets `1..=max` of the setup's **own** post (`setup::work_offset_names`, the cached table from slice 2). Each entry reads "Work offset n (NAME)", or "Work offset n" when the post gives that offset no name. The default post shows 6 entries. Tormach PathPilot shows 9 (G59.1-G59.3). If a setup holds a pick its post cannot express, for example offset 9 after switching to a six-offset post, that pick still shows as itself: "Work offset 9 - not on this post", listed alone after 1-6. It is never shown as offset 1. The post gate from slice 2 refuses it by setup name.
- **The wording is one function in app**: `setup_offsets::entry_label`.
- **Other UI words.** Slice 2 already moved the browser tree, the heights row, the viewport chips and the status line to the app's names. This slice changes the three texts that still named a fixed "G54-G59" range: the combo's hover, the heights page hint, and the WCS page's "Work offset:" line. The WCS page line appears in a release-lane snapshot, which gets regenerated at the cut; its structural twin `one_wcs` is updated here. I left the probe page's "Set G54".."Set G59" alone on purpose: the probe register arithmetic only reaches offsets 1-6 (triage point 4).
- **MCP `set_work_offset`** (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`):
  - It takes `index`, 1-based. The words `G54`-`G59` are accepted as aliases of 1-6.
  - `word` stays as the older spelling of the same argument. If both are given they must agree.
  - `setup_offsets::parse_index` checks only the shape and the 1-255 sanity bound. The post's range is checked by `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` → `setup_offsets::check`, so the refusal is the same one the GUI gives, by setup name.
  - Replies carry `index`, `name` and `word` (an alias of `name`). So do `set_wcs` and `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs` (`mcp/job.rs`).
- **camcraft-mcp skill doc**: documents the new `set_work_offset` arguments and replies.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` → 21**, because the skill doc changed. 21 is one above the highest bump in any open PR (20, #1033). **It renumbers at merge** if another process PR lands first. #681 needs the announcement when this merges.

  - `set_work_offset_takes_a_one_based_index_and_answers_index_name_and_word`

  - `the_combo_lists_the_setups_post_range_by_its_names`: 6 entries on the default post, 9 on Tormach
  - `a_pick_beyond_the_post_stays_visible_and_says_so`
- Updated: `an_unset_setup_reads_work_offset_one`, `the_picker_sets_the_setups_work_offset_through_the_command`, `offset_hint_names_the_real_pages_in_plain_words`, and the structural twin `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` (asserts the combo value is "Work offset 1 (G54)" and no bare word).

title: feat(post): work offsets ride the stream as a 1-based index; the post writes the word
body:
Slice 1 of 3 for #931: the post crate and scripts. Stacked on #945 (#934, Sinumerik G505/G506). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

**This changes the post interface** (what every script receives as `PARAM WorkOffset`), so it waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.

## What changed

- **The stream carries the index.** `dump` writes `PARAM WorkOffset` as the setup's 1-based offset number (`G55` -> `2`). App still hands the word and still caps at 6; slice 2 makes the `Dump` field an index.
- **New `workOffsetIndex` manifest flag** (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs`, on the `coolantModes` pattern). It is read once at load with `workOffsetMax` (6 when unstated):
  - A flagged script receives the number. The engine refuses an offset above its maximum by setup name.
  - An unflagged (user) script receives the word `G54`..`G59` for 1-6, exactly as before. Any offset above 6 is refused by setup name, and an unflagged script cannot raise its own maximum.
  - The legacy words `G54`..`G59` in a stream still read as 1-6. Any other value (`G53`, 0, 2.5, `G54.1 P3`) is refused by setup name before a script sees it.
  - `work_offset::work_offsets(cps)` returns the maximum and the `workOffsetName(n)` names for slice 2's display. It never feeds the stream.
- **All 11 scripts shipped when this was written** declare the flag (grblhal.cps and tinyg.cps, added to main later, do not yet: they stay on the unflagged path, offsets 1-6, follow-up #1385), `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName`, and map the index to their own word. No `slotOf` / `frameWord` / `frameOf` word parsing remains:
  - The Fanuc-family probe register reads `wcsIndex - 1`.
  - Sinumerik's `$P_UIFR[n]` uses the number directly.
  - Heidenhain maps offset n to preset row n.
- **Declared maxima:**
  - Tormach mill and Tormach lathe: **9** (`G59.1`..`G59.3`, cited to the LinuxCNC G-code reference: "G54-G59.3 Select Coordinate System (1 - 9)" and its G10 L2 table).
  - Every other dialect: **6**. Haas G154, Fanuc/Mazak/Doosan G54.1 P and further Sinumerik/Heidenhain frames or rows were not verified against a public manual, so none is written. Reasons and sources are in `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-post.md`.
- **Docs.** `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents the 1-based `WorkOffset` beside the probe's 0-based `SetWorkOffset` (triage point 4). `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes the flag, the maximum and the name function.

## Tests

- New `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` (9 tests). Every shipped script runs on recorded streams at offsets 1, 6, 7, its maximum and one past it, checking the word it writes or the refusal by setup name. It also covers:
  - a recorded generator toolpath (`face_square_40x40.cl`) through Fanuc and Tormach;
  - legacy word streams posting byte-identically to their index;
  - invalid values;
  - an unflagged user script at 1-6 and at 7, and one that tries to raise its maximum;
  - a flagged script without a maximum or names;
  - the dump writing the index;
  - each script's name table.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame` now expects the engine's refusal of `G53` (the engine refuses it before the script runs).
- Gate (local, worktree target, sccache), on head `2fe7afb7`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
  - 63 app suites, 431 passed, 0 failed. They cover every app suite that posts through the shipped scripts: conformance, golden_cl, posting, arc_planes, cli, the probe_* suites, sinumerik_*, heidenhain_*, fanuc_post, doosan_dnm_post, carvera_*, tormach_*, the lathe_post* suites, plasma_*, inverted_*, comment_escape, one_wcs, setups, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, rotated_wcs, setup_mounts_post, setup_post_options, per_op_files, program_comments, smoothing, after_op, coolant*, post_unit_word, regression_models, wear_comp, control_comp and lathe_spindle_law. There are no separate mazak or haas suites; those scripts are covered by conformance, fanuc_post and the inverted_* suites.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- 400-line law: the new manifest reading lives in its own module, `work_offset.rs`. `engine.rs` (511 -> 530 lines) and `js.rs` (409 -> 415) were already over 400 and grew only by the hook-up.

**Goldens:** no golden file changed. Offsets 1-6 post the same words as before.

**Not exercised:** the GUI and MCP (unchanged in this slice), a real control, and offsets above 6 end to end through app (app still caps at 6 until slice 2).

Changelog: Posts receive the work offset as a 1-based number and write their own word; the Tormach mill and lathe posts accept work offsets 7-9 (G59.1-G59.3), and a post that cannot express an offset refuses it by setup name (#931, slice 1)

title: fix(thread): refuse a hole the program ahead has not drilled
body:
Stacked on #1005 (refreshed against main at f3dd45c4; base branch content: `issue/894-thread-mill`). This PR targets `main`, so until #1005 merges its diff also shows #1005's commits - the #992 change is this branch's own commits only. **It must merge together with #1005, or right after it**: #1005's thread mill without this law posts a non-centre-cutting mill into an undrilled hole, and this PR does not build without #1005.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the #1005 ride feeds it down the hole's axis at plunge feed. Nothing checked that an earlier operation had opened the hole, so a forgotten tap drill posted a thread mill into solid metal. Now:

- **Generate refuses an undrilled hole by name** (`crates/app/src/operation/thread_entry.rs`, called from the Thread arm of `operation::generate`). Each threaded hole is read in the stock the setup's earlier operations leave standing - the same lazily cut prior grid the drilling and rapid laws read (`drill_prior::PriorCell`). The stock over the hole's minor circle (less one grid cell, never narrower than the mill) must stand at or below the lowest point the path takes the mill to in that hole. Otherwise: "the hole at (x, y) is not drilled yet: the stock the program ahead leaves stands at z .. inside it, above the thread mill's lowest point at z .. - a thread mill does not cut at its centre - add a drilling operation of at least the .. mm minor diameter, deep enough for its point, before the thread".
- **Unknown is refused, never read as air**: nothing ahead cut, a program ahead the grid cannot cut, a posed Thread, a distrusted carried prior, a hole off the grid.
- **Reordering**: an unposed op's stamp already digests the program ahead (#109), so moving the Drill after the Thread marks the Thread Stale, and regenerating it refuses. Pinned, no new stamp code.
- Test fixtures: the #894 thread suites' shared fixtures moved to `crates/app/tests/thread_support/mod.rs`. The modelled hole now runs to z 4 (the tap drill's depth), deeper than the thread's floor at z 8, and every thread there has a Drill operation ahead. `mill2d_c`'s R10 thread gets a 20 mm drill ahead. The MCP thread test now pins generate's refusal on the undrilled block.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/992-thread-undrilled.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-app --test thread_entry` (new, 5): `a_thread_with_nothing_drilled_ahead_is_refused_by_name`, `a_tap_drill_ahead_opens_the_hole_and_the_thread_verifies_clean` (generator verdict, post gate and program sim clean), `a_drill_of_the_mills_own_diameter_opens_the_hole_too`, `a_drill_too_narrow_or_too_shallow_is_refused`, `moving_the_drill_after_the_thread_marks_it_stale_and_refuses_it` (Stale, post gate shut, regeneration refused, undo restores Ok).
- `camcraft-app` (lib): `operation::thread_entry::tests::*` (4): drilled/exact-depth air, solid / shallow / narrow refusals by name, unknown prior and off-grid refusals, a hole the path never enters.
- Updated: `--test thread_mill` (all 8, now drilled first), `--test thread_mill_rim` (all 11) and `--test coarse_rims` thread test (main's #1071/#1073 thread tests: the hole is opened ahead by a flat end-mill Bore of the same declared holes), `--test hole_wall_flats` and `posted_gates/thread` (tap drill ahead), `--test mill2d_c` `thread_helices_are_timed_by_the_tools_pitch`, `--test mcp` `thread_milling_over_the_tools`.

Quick gate (refresh onto #1005 @ f3dd45c4 + upstream/main b0e29114, head `6dd3f773`): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` - tools, sim, motion, app (every suite) and ui suites, 5 steps, 0 failed (17.4 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (a test-only `Copy` lint fixed after the gate; `--test thread_mill_rim` re-run green, 11/11).

Goldens: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc` moved - the program now carries the Drill operation ahead (`G81 ... Z4 R20`) and the thread mill is T02; the thread's own blocks are byte-identical. No CL golden moved.

## What was not exercised

- A stock that already has the hole cored (a FromModel stock) with nothing ahead is refused, not acquitted (decision 3; cheap to add later).
- Posed (3+2) thread milling is refused by this law (no frame-aware prior reading).
- The milled Bore ride's axis entry has the same gap: filed as #1036.
- The heavy `--ignored` release lanes; posts other than Fanuc.

Changelog: A Thread operation whose hole the program ahead has not drilled (to the minor diameter, below the thread) is refused by name at generate instead of feeding a non-centre-cutting thread mill into solid stock (#992).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #992

title: feat(threadmill)!: thread-mill tool kinds and a reworked helical thread-milling operation
body:
## What changed

First slice of #894: thread mills can be stored, and an internal thread-milling operation verifies clean and posts helical G2/G3 with Z.

**Tool model**
- Two new tool kinds: `thread_mill` (multi-form: rows of teeth at one pitch) and `thread_mill_single` (single-form: one row, a pitch range). They read diameter (across the crests), form angle (`tip_angle`), `pitch`, cutting length (`flute_len`), flutes and shank; a single-form mill also reads the new `pitch_min` key. Sanity law, pitch door and form door live in `crates/tools/src/thread_mill.rs`.
- Library and project file round-trip (`pitch_min` is written only when set; additive, no project-version step), the tool editor (kind list, pitch / pitch range / form angle rows, a sane draft when the kind is picked), the tree's kind name, the operation digest, and two starter-catalog tools (`TM-0600-P125`, `TMS-0600-P050-150`).
- The program simulation sweeps a thread mill at its tooth roots, the reading a tap already has (#266).

**Thread operation** (the existing `Thread` kind, reworked)
- The kernel is rewritten (`machining2d/thread_mill.rs`, `thread_ride.rs`): radial passes are full helices (equal steps, the last on the thread depth), a single-form mill winds one turn per thread, a multi-form mill makes one revolution per level; tangential lead-in / lead-out arcs that keep the helix's axial rate; climb / conventional and right / left hand by the handbook rule; the tip never below the floor, no rapid below the feature's top; the feed stated at the cutting edge and programmed at the tool centre.
- New operation fields `pitch` (optional: unstated reads a multi-form mill's own) and `hand`; both in the file, the page (Passes tab) and the MCP `add_operation` / `edit_operation` params.
- Refusals by name when the operation is created, edited, retyped or re-tooled, and again at generate: a pitch outside a single-form mill's range, a pitch other than a multi-form mill's, a form angle other than 60 degrees, an infeed past the thread depth, a mill no smaller than a hole's minor diameter, a zero / negative / non-finite pitch. A single-form mill with the pitch not stated yet is an unfinished operation (a new Thread operation starts that way): it may be made and edited, and generate refuses it by name.
- Gouge laws (main's #1071 readings since the refresh, behind this PR's round-wall gate): the tooth crests are judged against the major circle of the model's own wall (`thread_rims::major_rims`, tangency law); the solid law keeps the full cutter and excuses only the thread's own wall and mouth inside that major cylinder (`verify::thread_bore`), at the thread's own pitch (`thread_op::bores`). Both apply only where every threaded hole is a round wall (`thread_op::walls_round`, #1205); otherwise the teeth are judged at full radius. The crossing law stands down for Thread only (successive passes' lead arcs cross in plan by design).

**Why the kernel was rewritten rather than extended** - on `main` no Thread operation can post: the old ride retraces itself (the crossing law convicts every pair) and stands past the hole rim (the tangency law convicts every move). It also deepened the radius turn by turn while descending, so the top threads were shallower than the bottom ones, and its "climb" wound counter-clockwise while descending, which is a left-hand helix. Details and sources: `docs/decisions/894-thread-mill.md`.

## Breaking

- A `Thread` operation no longer accepts a Tap-kind tool (`tool_law::THREAD_MILL` was `[Tap]`). An existing one shows the tool law's after-state and refuses to generate or post until its tool is re-kinded as a thread mill.
- Every existing `Thread` operation reads Stale once (its digest now carries pitch and hand) and regenerates to the new ride.
- `Tool` gains the field `pitch_min`: a branch that builds a full `Tool { .. }` literal needs `pitch_min: 0.0` after it merges main.

## How tested

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a; refreshed against upstream/main 0ad525d8 in merge `f3dd45c4`).

Gate on the final head `f3dd45c4`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (the diff falls back to the batch plan) - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app suites and clippy `-D warnings` over all eight crates: ok. The ui step failed one test on the first run (`tool_thread_mill_row` still named the thread mills' kind numbers 13 and 14; they are 14 and 15 after main's Electrode took 13); fixed in the test, and the ui step re-run as the gate runs it: 643 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored, the other ui binaries ok. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Thread suites on the head: `thread_mill` 8, `thread_mill_rim` 11 (main's #1071 pins, on the new kernel), `hole_wall_flats` 5, `solid_law_goldens` 7 (incl. `the_thread_golden_passes_its_gate` and `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`), `coarse_rims` 5, `mill2d_c` 9 - all passed.

Main moved once more after the merge (#1319, b0e29114, the verify's mid-turn sweep). It is not in this head; the PR merges with it cleanly, and a local trial merge passed the thread suites above plus `golden_cl` (29).

## Refresh against main (merge `f3dd45c4`, 27 conflicting files)

Most conflicts were both-sides-added lists (tool kinds, catalog, icons, UI rows, tests, `Tool` fields) and keep both. The judgements, recorded in `docs/decisions/894-thread-mill.md` ("The refresh against main"):

1. Region law: main's `major_rims` (#1071) replaces this PR's `crest_region` (main's circle grows from the model's own rim and is never wider), kept behind this PR's `walls_round` gate.
2. Solid law: main's thread grant with the full cutter replaces this PR's `root_cutter`, which credited the thread depth against every facet. The two are not stacked. `crest_region`, `root_cutter` and their unit tests are removed.
3. The grant reads the thread's own pitch (`thread_op::bores`): main passed `tool.pitch`, which on a single-form mill is only the coarsest of its range and would over-grant. Empty over a wall that is not round.
4. The crossing stand-down stays: tried off on the merged tree, 2 `thread_mill` and 5 `thread_mill_rim` tests convict.
5. Tool kind numbers: main's Electrode keeps 13, the thread mills take 14 and 15 (stamp digest in `stamp_tool.rs`, tool page list, `state.rs`).
6. Main's `thread_mill_rim.rs` and `coarse_rims.rs` mounted a Tap on a Thread op, which this PR refuses; they now mount a thread mill and state pitch and hand. No assertion changed.

No golden moved, no snapshot PNG, no process file.

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-tools` (lib): `thread_mill::tests::*` (4) - the two kinds' sanity, the pitch door, the form door.
- `camcraft-motion` (lib): `machining2d::thread_tests::*` (8) - hand and orbit sense for all 16 hand / climb / internal-external / form combinations, equal passes landing on the ISO depth, one shared helix across passes and levels, floor and no-rapid-below-top laws, the lead arcs' form law (a 60-degree tooth never leaves the groove), the centre-feed scaling, a boss never cut past its depth, the refusals.
- `camcraft-app` `--test thread_mill` (8): M8 x 1.25 with the multi-form mill and M8 x 1 with the single-form mill through the command path - no blocking warning, the post gate passes, the program simulation finds no gouge, Fanuc output carries `G03 ... Z ... I ...` blocks; left-hand and conventional variants; a mill whose roots meet the wall is a gouge; a bottom below the blind floor is a gouge; the creation-time refusals; a gated, undoable pitch edit; tool JSON and project-file round trip.
- `camcraft-app` (lib): `operation::thread_op::tests::*` (2) - the thread grant reads the thread's own pitch and only over a round wall, the crossing stand-down is Thread-only.
- `camcraft-app` `--test thread_mill_rim` (11, main's #1071 pins) and `--test hole_wall_flats` (5): a wider or off-centre declaration, a D-bore, an octagon, a 16-gon, a floor and a nearby wall convict; matched threads stay clean.
- `camcraft-app` `--test solid_law_goldens`: `the_thread_golden_passes_its_gate` (`posted_gates/thread.rs`).
- `camcraft-app` `--test mill2d_c`: the M2.4 C thread tests, updated to the new ride and tool kind.
- `camcraft-app` `--test mcp`: `thread_milling_over_the_tools`.
- `camcraft-ui` (lib): `egui_app::tool_thread_mill_row::tests::picking_a_thread_mill_kind_seeds_a_sane_tool_and_round_trips`, `egui_app::thread_mill_page_tests::the_thread_page_states_the_pitch_and_the_hand_and_apply_undoes`.
- `camcraft-app` `--test tool_gate` / `--test tool_law`: updated for the new kinds (the Thread row's catalog hint is now `TM-0600-P125`).

Goldens added (none moved):
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_internal_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_internal_multi_form_left_hand.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_external_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_m8_fine_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc`

## Known gap (read before merging)

- **An undrilled hole is not refused.** A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the ride feeds it down the hole's axis. Nothing yet checks that an earlier operation opened the hole: on a part whose hole is modelled, a Thread operation with no drilling before it generates and verifies clean. Before this PR no Thread operation could post at all, so this path is newly reachable. The check needs the stock the earlier operations leave standing (the grid `operation::drill_prior` reads) and is filed as #992 (`bug`, P1). The tests here thread a modelled hole in a solid stock box with no drill before it - they pin the ride and the part laws, not that entry.

## What was not exercised

- External threads at the operation level: the kernel cuts a boss and is pinned by tests and a golden, but the operation always passes `external: false` (no boss recognition or pick, and the static region cannot judge a tool beside a boss). Filed as #985.
- The thread form in the simulation and the tool preview: the stock sim removes the root cylinder only, and the tool draws as the cylinder its crests sweep. Filed as #986.
- Forms other than 60 degrees (Whitworth, NPT taper, trapezoidal) are refused, not cut. Filed as #987.
- Spring passes, unequal pass depths, a stated thread-depth override and M4 (left-hand cutter) climb sense. Filed as #988.
- Posts other than Fanuc were not run on a thread program; the inverted-machine post path already refuses a helical arc by name (`post/invert.rs`) and was not changed.
- The UI rows were compiled and unit-tested through the draft; no pixel snapshot was touched and the release-lane snapshot suite was not run.
- The heavy `--ignored` release lanes and the batch tier's clippy over untouched crates.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill text does not yet mention the new kinds and fields (a process file; it would need a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump). Filed as #989 (`MCP:`).

Changelog: Thread mills (multi-form and single-form) as tool kinds, and a reworked Thread operation that cuts internal threads by helical interpolation - radial passes, climb / conventional, right / left hand - verifies clean and posts G2/G3 with Z; breaking: a Thread operation no longer accepts a Tap-kind tool.

title: feat(post)!: the document's unit is the unit every post writes the program in
body:
#961 (its former parent) is merged; this branch has taken upstream/main.

**PathPilot Hub run (done 2026-11-12, 770MX sim):** `contour_plate_with_hole` inch (byte-identical to this branch's `golden/nc/inch/tormach/contour_plate_with_hole.nc`) ran to M30, 1:19, dimensions matching the mm reference. `drill_peck` inch alarmed `G73 Cannot feed with zero feed rate`: the fixture carries no feed/tool/spindle, the same in main's mm golden - filed as #1357, not caused here; #1357's own kit (T4 M6, F2.36) then passed. No inch program with rotary words was Hub-run.
Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed

The document's Units choice (`SetUnits`, already undoable and saved as `units`) is now also the unit every post writes the program in. One setting: the machine file's `units.length` no longer chooses anything; it only says what unit the file's own numbers are in.

- **Seam.** The app adds `Units: "mm" | "inch"` to `postOptions` on every post path (whole program, per-operation files, per-mount files) via `posting::program_options`. The stream stays mm. `post.exe` takes `--units mm|inch`.
- **Manifest law (`post::units`).** A script that can write inch declares `programUnits = "mm inch"`. An inch document on a script that doesn't is refused by name before any hook runs. This includes a user's own pre-#902 script. An unknown unit word is refused too.
- **Posts that write inch:** Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Doosan DNM (G20), and Siemens 840D (G700, the G710 twin). Lengths are written / 25.4 at four decimals and feeds in in/min at two. Angles, seconds and rpm are unchanged. The macro probe checks' band is one output step. The three Tormach posts now take the unit from the document instead of `machine.units`.
- **Posts that refuse inch by name:** Makera Carvera (its firmware is mm only), Heidenhain (#976) and Fanuc Lathe (#977). For Heidenhain and Fanuc Lathe, inch output needs verified dialect work, not a guess.

title: fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates
body:
**Changes posted G-code: waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.**

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a). Effort: high (safety floor: posted G-code; no escalation).

## What changed
- **One shared rule** - `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` (new, appended to the prelude every `.cps` sees): `rotaryRate(letter)` (stated feed speed, else rapid, deg/min), `rotaryFeedCap(f, lin, turns, mode)`, `rotaryFeed(p, prev, letters, mode, arc)` and `rotaryFeedWord(v)`. It caps F so no rotary runs past its stated rate and no linear part past `feedRateMax`, read the way the control reads F:
  - **path** - `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` under G43.4. F is the tool tip's speed relative to the work, with the rotaries carried along (FANUC 30i-B operator's manual, tool center point control): F <= rate x tip / |d|. With the tip still, F <= the rate.
  - **composite** - `doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` C-axis live tooling (#860). The control times the block over sqrt(lin^2 + sum d^2), counting degrees as mm (FANUC 0i-F operator's manual, feedrate for rotation axes). `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
  - **Arcs** that turn a rotary use the path rule over the chord in the arc's plane. That chord is never longer than any reading of an arc's F, so the cap is never too loose.
- A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A cap under 0.1 mm/min is refused by name.
- The post now tracks the angles the control holds (`rotAt`), taken only from the A/B/C words it actually wrote. If a feed turns a rotary from an angle the post never wrote, and that rotary states a rate, the post refuses it by name: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held`. Each rate refusal is counted once per program.
- An unstated rate caps nothing (the unstated-limit law).
- `tormach.cps` needs no cap: it writes A only on a G0 index and refuses an A that changes inside an operation (#785). haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse every tilted record.
- The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/885-rotary-feed-cap.md`.

## How tested
New pinning suite `crates/app/tests/rotary_feed_cap.rs`. It reads every posted motion block back, keeps the axes modal, and checks every feed block that turns A against the stated rates under that dialect's reading:
- `fanuc_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (pins `A30 F3.3`, `A60 F1000` and the uncapped `A61 F2000`)
- `doosan_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate`
- `doosan_fourth_axis_composite_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (also pins the refusal when no A word was ever written)
- `an_unstated_rate_caps_nothing`
- `a_feed_turning_from_an_unknown_angle_is_refused_by_name`

The lathe stays pinned by `c_axis_unwind::a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` and its golden, which did not change.

Gate (local, macOS, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` plus the 44 post-touching binaries: all green, 377 tests. The binaries are arc_planes, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, comment_escape, conformance, control_comp, coolant_followups, doosan_dnm_post, drill_prior, drill_rplane, fanuc_post, fourth_axis_pose, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_equivalence/post/probe, lathe_*, machine_library, plasma_*, post_unit_word, probe_*, program_comments, program_entry, rotary_feed_cap, turning_face_approach, vertical_arc_entry, wear_comp, tilt, rotary_verify, tormach_fourth_axis, microarc_test_part, tormach_machines and posting.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
**None.** No committed golden states a rotary rate on a tilted feed. The lathe's C-axis goldens (`c_axis_unwind.nc`, `c_axis_helix.nc`) are byte-identical through the shared rule.

## Test fixture changed
`fourth_axis_pose.rs` `tilted()` now opens with a rapid at the pose before its two feeds. Under the new refusal, its feeds would otherwise turn the shipped DNM 5700's rated A from an angle the post never placed. The tests' own assertions are unchanged.

## Not exercised
- No Hub run or machine cut yet.
- G93 inverse time is not implemented (see the decision file).
- Under G43.4 the machine's linear axes also make a compensating move that depends on the pivot length. No machine file states that length, so the control's own per-axis clamp covers it. The post caps the tip at `feedRateMax`.

## What changed

**Shared pick primitive** - `crates/app/src/pick/circle.rs` (next to the #692 pick graph): `circle_centre(world, &GeoSel)`, `circle_of_edge(graph, edge)`, `circle_of_run(features, run)` return a `Circle { centre, axis, radius, closed }` or a named `CircleRefusal` (`Straight`, `TooShort`, `NotCircular`, `NotAnEdge`, `Gone`). The edge pick resolves to its **run** (one straight stretch or one arc), so an arc of a filleted rim works too. The fit reuses `feature_arc::fit_arc` and its tolerances, and checks every vertex. A non-circular edge is refused, never guessed. The axis sign is canonical, so a hole in a top face reads +Z. The centre is in the active setup's view frame (#326), the frame the WCS is set in.

**Command + MCP** - `SetWcsAtCircleCentre` (`crates/app/src/commands/wcs_circle.rs`) resolves the circle when the command is created and wraps `SetWcsOrigin` at the centre: one undo step, and undo restores the previous origin. The MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre { edge: {model, id}, rotation? }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_circle.rs`) runs the same command and returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. The camcraft-mcp skill doc lists the tool. No MCP follow-up is needed.

**WCS page** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`, split out of the 1894-line `pages.rs`):
- Three collapsible sections: *Origin and orientation*, *Quarter turns* and *Anchor on*.
- The six value fields sit in a two-column grid, label and field on one row, with the fields in one column.
- The quarter turns are two rows of three equal buttons ([X+ Y+ Z+] / [X- Y- Z-]), plus *Level* and *Set Origin* as two equal halves. Every row spans the pane's width.
- The anchor grid is a 3x3 compass of equal cells (up to 72 x 30), placed exactly and centred.
- *Anchor on* has a third choice, **Circle centre**. It shows a "Pick a circular edge" toggle and then the result, e.g. "Circle Ø 20.00 mm, centre (0.00, 0.00, 10.00)", or "Not anchored: <reason>". While the toggle is armed, a viewport click takes feature edges only, one run per click, and hover highlights what a click would take. A landed pick disarms the toggle. Choosing Circle centre disarms the box markers, and the other way round.
- The Bottom/Middle/Top radios are now a plain "Z level" row. Beside the 120 px label column they widened the section past a narrow pane.

**Plumbing** - `CommandKind::SetWcsCircle`, and a new `state_wcs.rs` that also takes over the existing `SetWcs` arm (`state.rs` shrinks). The viewport routes clicks through `wcs_pick.rs` (anchor markers + circle pick), which shortens `interact.rs`. `feature_click::ask` returns the circle ask while armed.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/circle_centre.rs` (new, 5 tests) uses a plate with a drilled 8 mm hole (32 chords), off-centre at (5, -3):
  - `a_drilled_hole_rim_gives_its_true_centre_axis_and_radius`: centre within 1e-6, Ø 8, axis +Z, through a real ray pick, and again with the part moved.
  - `a_straight_edge_is_refused_by_name`.
  - `an_elliptical_rim_and_a_face_are_refused_never_guessed`: ellipse gives `NotCircular`, face gives `NotAnEdge`, stale id gives `Gone`.
  - `the_anchor_command_places_the_origin_and_undo_restores_the_previous_one`: undo, redo, and a refusal never builds a command.
  - `mcp_set_wcs_circle_centre_anchors_on_a_rim_and_refuses_a_straight_edge`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs` (structural, no pixels):
  - `the_page_has_three_sections_and_one_row_fields_in_one_column`
  - `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`
  - `the_anchor_points_are_a_centred_compass_of_equal_cells`
  - It also holds the three `turn_wcs` tests, moved verbatim from `pages.rs`. The test count is unchanged.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_circle_tests.rs`:
  - `a_rim_click_anchors_the_origin_on_its_centre_and_undo_restores_it`: combo, then the pick button, then a viewport click on a boss rim, then G54 at the centre. The page states the circle, and Undo restores (1, 2, 3).
  - `a_face_is_refused_by_name_and_lands_nothing`
- Gate (macOS, worktree target):
  - Ran green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `camcraft-app --lib`, the full `camcraft-ui` lib and integration suites (459 lib tests), and these app suites: circle_centre, feature_pick, feature_pick_wire, mcp, mcp_setup, mcp_pick, mcp_live, one_wcs, setup_wcs, commands_undo, wcs_align, wcs_view_pose, face_origin, vertex_pick, pick.

2. Set *Anchor on: Circle centre*, then press *Pick a circular edge*. Hovering a hole rim or boss edge should highlight it. A click should move the WCS origin to the circle centre at the rim's height and show "Circle Ø … , centre (…)". Ctrl+Z should restore the previous origin.

title: fix(ui,app): setup alignment composes on the current pose, one flow, readable picks (#738)
body:
## What changed (#738, maintainer-reported, P1)

1. **Moves compose on the current pose.** Laying on a face or on three points now computes the lay in the setup's current alignment and composes it onto that alignment, through new `pick::lay_on_plane_in` / `lay_on_points_in` and `setup_turn::held_centre`. Before, each move went back to the import pose first. Axes already composed. Each move is still one `AlignPartToSetup`, and one undo returns to the previous pose exactly. title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body: Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0. ## What changed - **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before. - **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name: - a number outside 1-9999; - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`. Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time. - **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves. - **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool. - **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md. - **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead. - **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set. **Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals. - **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `()`. - **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set. - **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment. - **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `% G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name. - **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N__MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set. title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Micron rounding of the words: the control's ladder can differ by under 1 µm.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
**Stacked on #437** (#418), which is on #433 (#417) and #432 (#416). Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the #419 work is 68bd14a5. Part of #363.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`
